title: Typo in appName documentation: "automatically it from" (missing word)
description:
The roxygen documentation for deployApp()'s appName parameter has a typo. A word appears to be missing:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/6c4cfa837c5c25d76cf6abdd8518c3d7658ae0f7/R/deployApp.R#L57-L59

 Location: R/deployApp.R, in the @param appName roxygen block (confirmed present as of commit 6c4cfa837c5c25d76cf6abdd8518c3d7658ae0f7). This propagates into the generated man/deployApp.Rd and the public reference docs at https://rstudio.github.io/rsconnect/reference/deployApp.html.

Suggested fix:

"If not specified, the first deployment will be automatically derived from the appDir for directory and website, and from the appPrimaryDoc for document."  

(Or whatever word was originally intended, e.g.,  "derived," "inferred," and "generated" are all plausible given the actual behavior in generateAppName(), but I can't determine from the source alone which was meant.)

title: Notify users when a new version of rsconnect is available
description:
This request is coming from a painful situation I encountered when I was using push-button deployment in RStudio. 

I'm on R version 4.4.1, for which CRAN only has prebuilt rsconnect binaries up to version 1.7.0. 

```
> install.packages("rsconnect")
Installing package into ‘/Users/zverham/Library/R/arm64/4.4/library’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
trying URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.4/rsconnect_1.7.0.tgz'
Content type 'application/x-gzip' length 822937 bytes (803 KB)
```

The actual current version of rsconnect is 1.10.0 - more recent versions of rsconnect use the v1 connect apis for publishing. The unversioned APIs have been removed from the product. 

This means that, for me, push-button deployment fails with the following error: 

```
Error in `POST()`:
! <http://localhost:3939/__api__/applications/3/upload> failed with HTTP
  status 404
404 page not found
Backtrace:
    ▆
 1. └─rsconnect::deployApp(...)
 2.   └─client$uploadApplication(application$id, bundlePath)
 3.     └─rsconnect:::POST(...)
 4.       └─rsconnect:::httpRequestWithBody(...)
 5.         └─rsconnect:::handleResponse(...)
 6.           └─rsconnect (local) reportError(response$content)
 7.             └─cli::cli_abort(...)
 8.               └─rlang::abort(...)
```

Without any clear indicator that (a) I'm on an out-of-date rsconnect version, or (b) that install.packages on its own won't give me the most recent rsconnect version. I have to either install from source or target a PPM repository that provides the prebuilt binary. 




The actual situation I was in has to do with how CRAN manages binary builds on older R versions (I think) - but one thing that would have made it easier to understand what was happening would be having rsconnect detect if a newer version exists and telling me.

title: writeManifest()/deployApp() installs BiocManager and contacts bioconductor.org for projects with no Bioconductor dependencies, breaking air-gapped deployments
description:
### Description

## Summary

Starting with rsconnect 1.10.0, dependency capture resolves Bioconductor repositories on every `writeManifest()`/`deployApp()` call, even when the project has no package with `Source == "Bioconductor"`. This installs BiocManager into the project library and validates the Bioconductor version online against `bioconductor.org`. In an air-gapped or offline environment the version check fails and capture stops, so CRAN-only content can no longer be published.

This is a regression from 1.8.0, where the Bioconductor repository list was only computed when a Bioconductor-sourced package was actually present.

## Expected behavior

A project whose dependencies are all from CRAN-like repositories should not install BiocManager or contact bioconductor.org during dependency capture.

## Actual behavior

On a CRAN-only renv project, `writeManifest()` installs BiocManager and then errors:

```
ℹ Capturing R dependencies from renv.lock
- Installing BiocManager ...
Error: invalid version specification 'unknown version: Bioconductor version cannot be validated; no internet connection?
    See #troubleshooting section in vignette'
```

## Root cause

In `R/bundlePackageRenv.R`, `parseRenvDependencies()` evaluates the Bioconductor repositories eagerly:

```r
bioc <- biocRepos(bundleDir)            # always runs, every deploy
if (any(bioc %in% repos)) {
  biocPkgs <- NULL
} else {
  biocPkgs <- availablePackages(bioc)
}
deps <- standardizeRenvPackages(renvLock$Packages, repos, biocPackages = biocPkgs)
```

`biocRepos()` calls `renv:::renv_bioconductor_repos()`, which installs BiocManager and resolves the Bioconductor version (a network call to `bioconductor.org/config.yaml`).

In 1.8.0 the same value was passed as a lazy argument and only forced for Bioconductor-sourced packages:

```r
deps <- standardizeRenvPackages(
  renvLock$Packages,
  repos,
  biocPackages = biocPackages(bundleDir)   # promise; only forced for Source == "Bioconductor"
)
```

The eager evaluation was introduced by commit 5ea5a31 ("fix bioconductor repository resolution", PR #1316), which is the PR that fixed issue #1314. `git tag --contains 5ea5a31` returns `v1.10.0` only, so this behavior is specific to the 1.10.0 release. Note that 1.9.0 was never published to CRAN; the CRAN archive goes directly from 1.8.0 (2026-04-10) to the current 1.10.0, so users upgrade from 1.8.0 straight into this behavior.

## Reproduction

1. R session with `repos` pointing only at a CRAN-like mirror (no Bioconductor repo), `R_BIOC_VERSION` unset.
2. A renv project whose renv.lock contains only CRAN packages.
3. Make `bioconductor.org` unreachable (simulate air gap), e.g. blackhole it in /etc/hosts.
4. Fresh R session, then `rsconnect::writeManifest()`.

Result: BiocManager is installed and capture fails with the version-validation error above.

## Suggested fix

Only resolve Bioconductor repositories when the project actually contains a Bioconductor-sourced package, restoring the lazy/conditional behavior from 1.8.0. Computing `bioc` only when needed avoids installing BiocManager and contacting bioconductor.org for CRAN-only content.

## Versions

- rsconnect 1.10.0 (affected). Last working: 1.8.0. 1.9.0 was never released to CRAN.
- Introduced by PR #1316 (commit 5ea5a31), the fix for issue #1314.
- renv (bundled Bioconductor resolution)
- BiocManager 1.30.27
- R 4.2, Linux x86_64



### Your environment

_No response_

title: improve history.dcf management
description:
~RStudio may not consume this information. If this is confirmed, remove the creation and maintenance of the history.dcf file.~

Workbench consumes the history.dcf (see WorkspacesApi.cpp).

We have observed a ~100G history.dcf and a ~200G history.new.dcf file.

A couple problems:

1. Do not grow forever.
2. Do not add duplicates.

Duplicate calls to `saveDeployment()` happen naturally during `deployApp()`. The regular `writeDeploymentRecord()` save overwrites previous data. The deployment history file only prepends (by writing to a copy before overwriting the original).

We still do not know what caused this particular user history to double in size (with what appeared to be a single update, but that is speculation).

title: Allow deployments using records from the lockfile data itself (no local sync check)
description:
PR https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/1318 helps alleviate the problem where lockfile and local library are out of sync by ignoring the lockfile and use only local library DESCRIPTION data.

Still, on the other hand, there are still valid use cases where the existing lockfile should be enough to allow a deployment without the need of the local system packages to be in sync.

We can build DESCRIPTION-like records from the lockfile data itself,  the lockfile has `Package, Version, Source, Repository, and remote` fields. We could synthesize a minimal description record from those fields without needing the package to be locally installed at all. This is what is asked for in #1046 was asking for ("the renv.lock file should have all the information we need").

This is a cleaner long-term solution and what truly solves the CI/CD use case (no library needed at all), but it's a bigger change (thus #1318 helping on the short term) we'd need to confirm that Connect doesn't depend on any DESCRIPTION fields beyond what the lockfile provides.

title: Feature Request: Option to bypass local-to-lockfile sync check in deployApp()
description:
I'm developing a shiny app contained within a package, and want to deploy the shiny app to shinyapps.io via {rsconnect}. In order for the deployment to be successful, all the dependencies of the package and the package itself need to be listed in the renv.lock file, so it can be installed.

{renv} itself cannot natively allow this to happen (https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/2285), so my workaround attempt was to manually add the package to the renv lockfile using `renv::record()`. Then I ran into this error during deployment:

```
ℹ Capturing R dependencies from renv.lock
Error in `parseRenvDependencies()`:
! Library and lockfile are out of sync
ℹ Use renv::restore() or renv::snapshot() to synchronise
ℹ Or ignore the lockfile by adding to your .rscignore
Backtrace:
    ▆
 1. └─rsconnect::deployApp(...)
 2.   └─rsconnect:::bundleApp(...)
 3.     └─rsconnect:::createAppManifest(...)
 4.       └─rsconnect:::bundlePackages(...)
 5.         └─rsconnect:::computePackageDependencies(...)
 6.           └─rsconnect:::parseRenvDependencies(lockfile, bundleDir)
 7.             └─cli::cli_abort(...)
 8.               └─rlang::abort(...)
Execution halted
```

It appears that when deploying an app, if rsconnect notices that I have my own lockfile, rsconnect attempt to do its own dependency check and verify that they are in sync. This check fails. But if deployApp() would use the provided renv lockfile that I have, it should work.

It would be helpful if there was a way to disable the sync check. I'm currently stuck and unsure how to deploy my shiny app that's inside a package.

title: manifest chooses wrong repository for bioconductor packages in transit
description:
### Description

**Summary**

When using `rsconnect` to create a manifest file for a project that includes Bioconductor packages that happen to be available in CRAN's transit directory, the manifest will get the wrong value for "Repository"

**Repro**
Create a shiny app that uses `S4Vectors` from Bioconductor.

```r
# Session state: R 4.5.3, Posit Cloud, BiocManager 3.22 repos configured.
# S4Vectors 0.48.1 installed from Bioconductor.

options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cran.rstudio.com/"))
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "rsconnect"))
BiocManager::install(c("S4Vectors"))
packageDescription("S4Vectors")$Version
#> [1] "0.48.1"

# See what rsconnect finds
ap <- rsconnect:::availablePackages(getOption("repos"))
ap["S4Vectors", c("Version", "Repository")]
#> Version                                          Repository
#> "0.49.1-1"    "https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/Transit"

rsconnect:::findRepoUrl("S4Vectors", ap)
#> [1] "https://cran.rstudio.com"
```

Resulting `manifest.json` entry:

```json
"S4Vectors": {
  "Source": "Bioconductor",
  "Repository": "https://cran.rstudio.com",
  "description": { "Version": "0.48.1", "Repository": "Bioconductor 3.22", "...": "..." }
}
```

`https://cran.rstudio.com` doesn't serve S4Vectors 0.48.1. Only the Transit copy at 0.49.1-1 is there, under a different URL. Any deploy target that takes this manifest literally will fail the install.

**Root cause**

Peeking into the Packages on each repository, first you can see Bioconductor has version 0.48.1
Value from https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/src/contrib/PACKAGES
```
Package: S4Vectors
Version: 0.48.1
Depends: R (>= 4.0.0), methods, utils, stats, stats4, BiocGenerics (>=
        0.53.2)
Suggests: IRanges, GenomicRanges, SummarizedExperiment, Matrix,
        DelayedArray, ShortRead, graph, data.table, RUnit, BiocStyle,
        knitr
License: Artistic-2.0
MD5sum: 97d42c8c8d6bf44fd95675b48dc66d1e
NeedsCompilation: yes
```

Next you can see CRAN has version 0.49.1-1 in Transit, pinned to `(R (>=4.6.0)`
Value from https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/PACKAGES
```
Package: S4Vectors
Version: 0.49.1-1
Depends: R (>= 4.6.0), methods, utils, stats, stats4, BiocGenerics (>=
        0.53.2)
Suggests: IRanges, GenomicRanges, SummarizedExperiment, Matrix,
        DelayedArray, ShortRead, graph, data.table, RUnit, BiocStyle,
        knitr
License: Artistic-2.0
MD5sum: 1f9b83fd10000c017015e8e9f1af4860
NeedsCompilation: yes
Path: Transit
```

Two pieces interact to produce the bad output.

1. `rsconnect:::availablePackages()` in `R/bundlePackage.R` passes a narrower `filters` argument than R's default:

    ```r
    availablePackages <- function(repos) {
      # note that we explicitly exclude the "R_version" filter as we want to ensure
      # that packages which require newer versions of R than the one currently
      # in use can still be marked as available on CRAN -- for example, currently
      # the package "foreign" requires "R (>= 4.0.0)" but older versions of R
      # can still successfully install older versions from the CRAN archive
      filters <- c(
        getOption("rsconnect.available_packages_filters", default = c()),
        "duplicates"
      )
      available.packages(repos = repos, type = "source", filters = filters)
    }
    ```

    R's default is `c("R_version", "OS_type", "subarch", "duplicates")`. rsconnect's override is just `"duplicates"`, which means rows that would otherwise be dropped by `R_version` (packages declaring an R dependency newer than the current session) stay in the matrix.

    The side effect of that choice is that CRAN Transit builds also stay visible even though the depend on a higher version of R than used in this session:

    ```r
    options(repos = BiocManager::repositories())
    ap_default <- available.packages(type = "source")                       # default filters
    ap_rsconnect <- available.packages(type = "source", filters = "duplicates") # rsconnect's

    ap_default[ap_default[,"Package"]=="S4Vectors", "Repository"]
    #> "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.22/bioc/src/contrib"

    ap_rsconnect[ap_rsconnect[,"Package"]=="S4Vectors", "Repository"]
    #> "https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/Transit"
    ```

    The Transit row only becomes visible once the `R_version` filter is dropped.

2. `rsconnect:::findRepoUrl` then picks the first `Package`-name hit in that matrix, with no version awareness:

    ```r
    function(pkg, availablePackages) {
      idx <- match(pkg, availablePackages[, "Package"])
      if (!is.na(idx)) {
        repo <- availablePackages[[idx, "Repository"]]
        gsub("/src/contrib.*$", "", repo)
      } else {
        NA_character_
      }
    }
    ```

    With `"duplicates"` already having collapsed multiple rows for the same package to the highest-version row, `findRepoUrl` returns whichever Repository URL that row happened to carry. The combination of "keep extra rows visible" plus "pick by name only" is leads to a CRAN Transit URL in a Bioc manifest entry.

    Note I'm not sure this requires the `R_version` filter to be dropped. Transit rows whose R requirement happens to match the current session (e.g. Rcpp, S7, precondition at the moment) collide the same way even under default filters. But dropping `R_version` expands the set of packages that can collide from "only those whose Transit build matches the session's R" to "any package currently in Transit," which is how I hit the Bioconductor case.

**Proposed fix**

Two options, not mutually exclusive.

**Bioconductor fix: swap the lookup order in `standardizeRenvPackage`'s Bioconductor branch.**

The function already receives a separate `biocPackages` matrix alongside the combined `availablePackages`, but only consults it if the packages isn't otherwise found:

```r
else if (pkg$Source == "Bioconductor") {
    pkg$Repository <- findRepoUrl(pkg$Package, availablePackages)
    if (is.na(pkg$Repository)) {
        pkg$Repository <- findRepoUrl(pkg$Package, biocPackages)
    }
}
```

Consulting `biocPackages` first would resolve the specific collision in this report:

```r
else if (pkg$Source == "Bioconductor") {
    pkg$Repository <- findRepoUrl(pkg$Package, biocPackages)
    if (is.na(pkg$Repository)) {
        pkg$Repository <- findRepoUrl(pkg$Package, availablePackages)
    }
}
```

**Broader fix?: make the lookup version-aware.**

The Bioconductor swap only fixes one branch. The same `findRepoUrl(pkg$Package, ...)` call appears in four other places (`R/bundlePackageRenv.R:118`, `:137`, `:159`, and the packrat path at `R/bundlePackagePackrat.R:91`, `:95`), and they all have this same theoretical issue: they look up a package by name and trust whatever Repository URL comes back, even if it points to a different version than what's installed. Transit is the obvious trigger, but the same mismatch can happen any time a package appears in more than one configured repo at different versions.

The fix would be to match on package *and* version, not just name. Two things would need to change together: `availablePackages()` would need to stop dropping rows via the `"duplicates"` filter (since those are the rows you'd be disambiguating against), and `findRepoUrl()` would need to take a version argument. Callers already have `pkg$Version` on hand, so passing it through is the easy part. The harder questions are what to do when no row matches the installed version (the CRAN-archive case the existing comment is guarding against), and whether keeping the wider matrix breaks anyone using the `rsconnect.available_packages_filters` option.

**Impact**

Affects any `rsconnect` user whose local CRAN currently lists a Transit row for a package they have installed from a different source. 

**Environment**

- rsconnect: `<your version>` (run `packageVersion("rsconnect")`)
- R 4.5.3, Posit Cloud, Ubuntu Noble
- BiocManager 3.22


### Your environment

_No response_

title: Deploying with renv profiles uses wrong lockfile
description:
### Description

When deploying a project that uses an renv profile, `deployApp()` fails with "Library and lockfile are out of sync" even though `renv::restore()` confirms the library is synchronized. The issue is that `bundleAppDir()` copies project files into a temp staging directory, and the renv/ directory is excluded from bundling (as expected). But when using an renv profile like 'dev', the profile-specific lockfile lives at renv/profiles/dev/renv.lock, so it gets excluded too. Only the root renv.lock (from the default profile) ends up in the bundle.

Later, `parseRenvDependencies()` reads this default-profile lockfile and compares versions against the library, which has packages from the active profile. The versions don't match, producing the error.

title: Disable shinyapps.io log streaming
description:
The shinyapps.io backend does not truly support log streaming and has not for many years.
We should update the code and documentation to accurately reflect this; it may have semi-worked but only via continual polling of the same last log line. This will also address backend load issues.

title: refactor: use httr2 utilities to parse and construct URLs and query params
description: The "URL manipulation" and "Helpers" sections of http.R can mostly be offloaded to httr2, it appears, even when using the libcurl backend. That should also allow some refactoring and simplification of some requests, like those that manually construct query strings.

title: Confirm that httr2 just handles cookies as needed
description: See https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/1284/files#r2653726756 and linked issues. We shouldn't need to maintain our own cookie store in this package.

title: Remove non-libcurl backends
description:
These were deprecated in #762 (March 2023), and the news bullet said "The old backends will remain available for at least 2 years." We're coming up on 3 years now. There are no open issues that suggest problems with libcurl, so they should be safe to remove. 

Maybe once we axe those, we can migrate to `httr2` and offload even more responsibility to well tested and maintained libraries.

title: RCurl is still a required dependency in some workflow and not just a Suggest.
description:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/9722f484982ba18c707d2ea12a31dc4c59efc99b/R/http.R#L498-L503

Here `RCurl` is used, but it is a Suggest only 
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/9722f484982ba18c707d2ea12a31dc4c59efc99b/DESCRIPTION#L38-L46

However, it is used in the process of `rsconnect::ConnectCloudUser()`. 

See traceback while using this function inside `publish_book()`

````
 1. ├─xfun::in_dir("docs", bookdown::publish_book("blogdown-book-test"))
  2. ├─bookdown::publish_book("blogdown-book-test")
  3. │ └─rsconnect::connectCloudUser()
  4. │   └─rsconnect:::waitForDeviceAuth(authClient, deviceAuth)
  5. │     ├─base::tryCatch(...)
  6. │     │ └─base (local) tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
  7. │     │   └─base (local) tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
  8. │     │     └─base (local) doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
  9. │     └─authClient$exchangeToken(...)
 10. │       ├─base::paste0(content, "&device_code=", urlEncode(request$device_code))
 11. │       └─rsconnect:::urlEncode(request$device_code)
````

It will use `urlEncode()` which requires curl. Should `curl::curl_escape()` be used ? 

Currently the error is 
````
Error in `loadNamespace()`:
! there is no package called ‘RCurl’
`````

Full example with `rsconnect::connectCloudUser()` directly

`````
> rsconnect::connectCloudUser()
ℹ Opening login page - confirm the code entered matches the code: HXQB-QGCF.
Error in `loadNamespace()`:
! there is no package called ‘RCurl’
Hide Traceback
Fix
Explain
     ▆
  1. ├─rsconnect::connectCloudUser()
  2. │ └─rsconnect:::waitForDeviceAuth(authClient, deviceAuth)
  3. │   ├─base::tryCatch(...)
  4. │   │ └─base (local) tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
  5. │   │   └─base (local) tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
  6. │   │     └─base (local) doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
  7. │   └─authClient$exchangeToken(...)
  8. │     ├─base::paste0(content, "&device_code=", urlEncode(request$device_code))
  9. │     └─rsconnect:::urlEncode(request$device_code)
 10. └─base::loadNamespace(x)
 11.   └─base::withRestarts(stop(cond), retry_loadNamespace = function() NULL)
 12.     └─base (local) withOneRestart(expr, restarts[[1L]])
 13.       └─base (local) doWithOneRestart(return(expr), restart)
````

This prevent a smooth experience for migrating from bookdown.org by letting `publish_book()` running the account connection for the user.

title: Objects not found after deploying to shinyapps.io despite app working on local machine

Hello,

I have tried a few times to deploy an app that was working well on my local machine to shinyapps.io via rsconnect.  I run the deployApp code on my own machine after setting up the link to my lab's shinyapps.io account, and the code runs to completion and tells me the app is successfully deployed.  However, the webpage throws an error when I try to click on the link to the app.  When I check the logs in shinyapps.io, it looks like some objects that are loaded into the environment with my app.R code (or created from loaded-in objects) are not found.  There's also a warning message about reticulate, but I don't think that's the main problem, as it looks like the app starts after that warning line. title: Using a manifest.json file with the deploy*() functions. Docs unclear.
description:
Initially I expected that the manifest file created using `writeManifest()` would be the thing that gets used when deploying an app.

My intended workflow was to have a script generating a manifest.json file, essentially constructing a customized list of files to be included in the bundle before calling `writeManifest(appFiles=files)`.

After trying to deploy a shiny app with `deployApp()` to a Posit connect server and getting some weird errors, I downloaded the bundle and quickly noticed that the manifest wasn't the one I generated. The unintended inclusion of files was the cause of these errors. 
The docs are really unclear on this. What is the purpose of generating a custom `manifest.json` and checking it into my repo if `deployApp()` regenerates it from scratch anyway?

Is there anyway to actually deploy based on an existing manifest file?
The python package `rsconnect-python` seems to enable this in a straightforward way, but I cannot  figure it out here.

title: RStudio account registration broken in 1.6.0
description:
The following error can occur when using the RStudio publishing preferences to configure a Connect account:

```
Error in rsconnect:::registerUserToken(serverName = serverName, accountName = accountName,  : 
  argument "accessToken" is missing, with no default
```

The error appears in the R console, while a separate UI dialog contains the following text:

> **Account Connect Failed**
>
> Your account was authenticated successfully, but could not be connected to RStudio. Make sure your installation of the 'rsconnect' package is correct for the server you're connecting to.
>
> Server: SERVERNAME (https://SERVERNAME/__api__)
> Version: 
> About: 
>
> Error occurred while executing method

The underlying cause is that `registerUserToken` gained arguments without defaults.

Called by RStudio.
https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/main/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionRSConnect.R

Neither `accessToken` nor `refreshToken` have default values and RStudio / Workbench do not know about this change (already-released RStudio only ever knows about the old signature).

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/f0938ee844cc335fbce7ff9a73edfa8911da9fef/R/ide.R#L49-L67

Arrived in https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/1217/files#diff-ae71c8761e556da984fb942359a2ca6a5849c4c3f83f58098cbe52357d8b61be

title: Require requirements.txt when deploying reticulated content to Connect
description:
tl;dr: rsconnect should require a requirements.txt for reticulated content, and offer some guidance about how to generate it. 

background: `py_require()` is the recommended way for reticulated projects to declare dependencies. reticulate will then resolve those dependencies at runtime into an ephemeral environment.

The behavior of rsconnect, when deploying to Connect, will differ depending on whether the content has been run locally before deploying or not:

> 1. If they run their code and hit all of the py_require functions before deploying, things will work as expected.  Reticulate will have set the VIRTUAL_ENV variable and Connect will know where to look to find all the Python dependencies.
> 2. If a user is working in a fresh R session, Connect will not realize that this deployment requires Python. No Python or packages will be installed, and instead when the application runs in Connect, uv will dynamically install everything.

Connect has separate processes for building and running content. This separation needs to be maintained in order to support other existing features (such as the API endpoint that lists what dependencies & versions are used by which pieces of content). Resolving dependencies and building an environment at runtime breaks this model, so we don't want to use the ephemeral environments on Connect. 

Ideally rsconnect would be able to detect the use of ephemeral environments and give some specific guidance about how to materialize them. Unfortunately however, it is not possible to detect whether a local project uses ephemeral environments except by running it up until the point where it initializes Python and then checking `reticulate:::is_epheremal_venv_initialized()`. This won't work for rsconnect: we can't assume the user has run the code in their session before they try to deploy (and indeed the push-button deploy in RStudio happens in a separate process, so definitely won't have run the content).

After some discussion it seems like the thing to do is for rsconnect to require a requirements.txt for reticulated content. Connect can use this to build the environment in its normal way and prevent the runtime dependency resolution from occurring. If a requirements.txt is not present, rsconnect should fail fast with an error that gives some guidance as to how to generate the requirements.txt file.

See also: 
* https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/1143
* https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/issues/1832
* https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/issues/538

title: python discovery for reticulate can cause inspection errors
description:
> related also to this issue and maybe this is just more details on this specific issue.
> 
> When you try to deploy an app that has ragnar as a dependency AND you have used ragnar in a way that generated the ephemeral python environment as described in the original issue, you get the following error during deployment to Connect.
> 
> 
> ℹ Capturing R dependencies from renv.lock
> ✔ Found 72 dependencies
> Error in `pythonConfig()`:
> ! Failed to detect python environment
> Caused by error in `system2()`:
> ! error in running command
> Backtrace:
>      ▆
>   1. ├─rsconnect::deployApp(...)
>   2. │ └─rsconnect:::bundleApp(...)
>   3. │   └─rsconnect:::createAppManifest(...)
>   4. │     └─rsconnect (local) pythonConfig(appDir)
>   5. │       ├─base::withCallingHandlers(...)
>   6. │       └─rsconnect:::inferPythonEnv(appDir, python = python, forceGenerate = forceGenerate)
>   7. │         └─base::system2(...)
>   8. └─rsconnect (local) `<fn>`(`<cmdError>`)
>   9.   └─cli::cli_abort("Failed to detect python environment", parent = err)
>  10.     └─rlang::abort(...)
> Execution halted
> 
> This happens because python is retrieved by the `getPython` function when the option of `"rsconnect.python.enabled` is set to `TRUE`.
> ```
>     pythonEnabled <- getOption("rsconnect.python.enabled", !targetIsShinyapps)
>     if (pythonEnabled) {
>         getPython(path)
> ```
> 
> The function `rsconnect::inferPythonEnv` uses the value of `python = getPython()`, which will return NULL in this case, since it is just using the call `Sys.getenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON")`. The method used by `reticulate` described in the original issues above does not set any environment variables.  Additionally, conda is not used in this case either. 
> 
> The way `inferPythonEnv` works, is shown below:
> 
> ```
> rsconnect:::inferPythonEnv
> function (workdir, python = getPython(), forceGenerate = FALSE) 
> {
>     env_py <- system.file("resources/environment.py", package = "rsconnect")
>     args <- c(shQuote(env_py), if (forceGenerate) "-f", shQuote(workdir))
>     hasConda <- is_installed("reticulate") && reticulate::py_available(initialize = FALSE) && 
>         reticulate::py_config()$anaconda
>     if (hasConda) {
>         prefix <- getCondaEnvPrefix(python)
>         conda <- getCondaExeForPrefix(prefix)
>         args <- c("run", "-p", prefix, python, args)
>         output <- system2(command = conda, args = args, stdout = TRUE, 
>             stderr = NULL, wait = TRUE)
>     }
>     else {
>         output <- system2(command = python, args = args, stdout = TRUE, 
>             stderr = NULL, wait = TRUE)
>     }
> ```
> 
> So when python is NULL and conda is not used, the `system2(command = python, ....` will fail with the error I pasted above.
> 
> It is interesting, since in logical case where conda exists, the python is extracted from the `reticulate::py_config()$anaconda` variable.
> 
> So perhaps the `inferPythonEnv` function should instead be using the `reticulate::py_config()$python` location when `reticulate` is installed, like this? 
> 
> ```
>     hasVirtualEnv <- is_installed("reticulate") && reticulate::py_available(initialize = FALSE) && 
>         !reticulate::py_config()$anaconda
>   
>    if(hasVirtualEnv) python <- reticulate::py_config()$python
> 
> ```
> Since `reticulate` is already a suggested package, and in this case, you are already checking for `reticulate` being installed, perhaps this logical case would properly find the python reticulate is using in a cleaner way?
> Tagging @t-kalinowski, @aronatkins and @nealrichardson since I discussed this issue with them. 
> 
>  

 _Originally posted by @SokolovAnatoliy in [#1143](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/1143#issuecomment-3310413166)_

title: addServer without snowflakeConnectionName prevents successful registration in same R session
description:
In a new R session:
 
1. Attempt to `addServer` without `snowflakeConnectionName`. Fails as expected.
2. Attempt to `addServer` with `snowflakeConnectionName`. Unexpectedly fails.

```r
# Incorrect attempt to configure a server hosted in Snowflake
rsconnect::addServer('https://the-hostname.snowflakecomputing.app', 'the-hostname')
# Corrected attempt to configure a server hosted in Snowflake, but continues to fail
rsconnect::addServer('https://the-hostname.snowflakecomputing.app', 'the-hostname', snowflakeConnectionName='the-connection')
```

Something about the initial failed `addServer` call is preventing a subsequent call to `addServer` from succeeding.


In a new R session:
 
1. Attempt to `addServer` with `snowflakeConnectionName`. Succeeds as expected.

```r
# From a fresh R session, the server is successfully added.
rsconnect::addServer('https://the-hostname.snowflakecomputing.app', 'the-hostname', snowflakeConnectionName='the-connection')
```

Workaround is to restart the R session before calling `addServer` with the correct arguments.

title: Add tests for `connectClient()`
description:
The Connect client object is not tested.

There was an old test that was labeled "Users API" but tested the entire Connect object workflow. It was deleted in #1183 and is pasted below. Perhaps using this as a starting point makes sense.

```r

test_that("Users API", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_on_os("windows")
  skip("connect user test skipped.")

  ## rm db/*.db
  server <- serverInfo(findServer())

  connect <- connectClient(server$url, list())
  id <- paste(as.hexmode(sample(256, bytes) - 1), collapse = "")

  # add a user
  record <- userRecord(
    email = paste0("user", id, "@gmail.com"),
    username = paste0("user", id),
    first_name = "User",
    last_name = "Resu",
    password = paste0("password", id)
  )

  response <- connect$addUser(record)

  # check a couple main fields
  expect_equal(
    response[c("email", "first_name", "last_name", "username")],
    list(
      email = record$email,
      first_name = record$first_name,
      last_name = record$last_name,
      username = record$username
    )
  )

  # make sure we returned an empty password field (or no password field?)
  expect_true(response$password %in% "" || is.null(response$password))

  # generate a token
  accountId <- response$id
  token <- generateToken()

  tokenResponse <- connect$addToken(list(
    token = token$token,
    public_key = token$public_key,
    user_id = accountId
  ))

  Sys.sleep(1)

  # open the URL in the browser
  utils::browseURL(tokenResponse$token_claim_url)

  # Sleep for a second so we can be sure that automatic auth happened
  Sys.sleep(2)

  # finally, create a fully authenticated client using the new token, and
  # keep trying to authenticate until we're successful
  connect <- connectClient(
    service = server$url,
    authInfo = list(token = token$token, private_key = token$private_key)
  )

  repeat {
    tryCatch(
      {
        user <- connect$currentUser()
        break
      },
      error = function(e, ...) {
        # we expect this to return unauthorized until the token becomes active,
        # but bubble other errors
        if (length(grep("401 - Unauthorized", e$message)) == 0) {
          stop(e)
        }
        Sys.sleep(1)
      }
    )
  }

  # Create and remove an example application

  ## Create it
  splineReticulator <- connect$createApplication("SplineReticulator")

  # Update the account id (since we have moved from unauthed user
  # to authed user)
  accountId <- splineReticulator$user_id

  ## Confirm it exists
  apps <- connect$listApplications(accountId)
  app <- apps[[which(sapply(apps, `[[`, "id") == splineReticulator$id)]]
  expect_true(app$name == "SplineReticulator")

  ## Upload a bundle
  pwd_splat <- strsplit(getwd(), "/")[[1]]
  if (pwd_splat[length(pwd_splat)] == "rsconnect") {
    path <- "tests/testthat/test-shinyApp/test-shinyApp.tar.gz"
  } else {
    path <- "test-shinyApp/test-shinyApp.tar.gz"
  }

  response <- connect$uploadApplication(
    splineReticulator$id,
    normalizePath(path = path)
  )

  ## Deploy an application
  appId <- response$app_id
  response <- connect$deployApplication(list(id = appId))
  id <- response$id

  ## Query the app for success / failure
  response <- connect$waitForTask(id)

  ## Terminate the application (does not remove it from store)
  connect$terminateApplication(appId)

  apps <- connect$listApplications(accountId)
  expect_false(response$id %in% sapply(apps, "[[", "id"))
})
```

title: Problem finding rsconnect package in a docker image where the latest version 1.5 is being installed
description:
We started hitting an error with our [shiny deploy tests](https://github.com/rstudio/lucid-selenium/tree/main/tests/shinyapps_api) with the latest version of rsconnect that gets installed in our dockerfile built on top of `rocker/r-ver`

Confirmed that pinning back to version rsconnect 1.4.2 makes our failures go away.  This could be an issue with our test setup that happens to break with the latest update, but thought I should log for investigation just in case.


```
Error (test-deploy-to-shinyapp-io.R:5:1): (code run outside of `test_that()`)
<packageNotFoundError/error/condition>
Error in `loadNamespace(x)`: there is no package called ‘rsconnect’
Backtrace:
    ▆
 1. └─base::loadNamespace(x) at test-deploy-to-shinyapp-io.R:5:1
 2.   └─base::withRestarts(stop(cond), retry_loadNamespace = function() NULL)
 3.     └─base (local) withOneRestart(expr, restarts[[1L]])
 4.       └─base (local) doWithOneRestart(return(expr), restart)
```


fwiw, it appears to build the image without any errors and shows that rsconnect is successfully installed.
also, if it matters we are using the [testthat](https://testthat.r-lib.org/) framework for this test.

title: curl_fetch_memory error on curl 6.3.0
description:
When running `rsconnect::setAccountInfo`, I receive the following error:

```
> rsconnect::setAccountInfo(name='asdfasdf', token='blah', secret='blah')
Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : 
  SSL connect error [api.shinyapps.io]: TLS connect error: error:0BFFF065:x509 certificate routines:CRYPTO_internal:cert already in hash table
```

This looks to be an incompatibility with the latest version of the curl package, `6.3.0` - this works fine after installing `6.2.3`. Its [NEWS](https://github.com/jeroen/curl/blob/master/NEWS) makes reference to a libcurl upgrade to 8.14.1 and a change to mac-native LibreSSL:

```
 - MacOS/Windows: update to libcurl 8.14.1 
 - MacOS: our static build of libcurl now links to the MacOS native LibreSSL
   and nghttp in order to use the same keychain certificates as native curl.
```

I'm able to reproduce this on MacOS - not sure if this is also an issue on Windows.

title: Wrong error when no accounts have been registered
description:
This is a relatively simple fix, but I realized I was getting a strange error when trying to find which accounts are registered in our rsconnect server. 

```
pins:::rsc_server_rsconnect("https://rsconnect.ourserver.com")
Error in `arg_match0()`:
! `values` must have at least one element.
```

When checking the function that was actually returning the error I saw:

```
rsc_server_rsconnect <- function (server = NULL, name = NULL) 
{
  check_installed("rsconnect")
  accounts <- rsconnect::accounts()
 if (is.null(accounts)) {
    abort("No Posit Connect servers have been registered")
  }
  if (!is.null(server)) {
    server <- arg_match0(server, accounts$server, "server")
    accounts <- accounts[accounts$server == server, , drop = FALSE]
  }
```
Here the check ` if (is.null(accounts))` will return FALSE even if there are no accounts registered, because `rsconnect::accounts()` does not return NULL, but an empty `data.frame` when there are no accounts.  

The fix is likely quite simple, just check the number of rows ` if (nrow(accounts) == 0)` or something of the sort.

title: Implement flags for targeting an execution environment during deployment
description:
Connect 2025.04 allows setting `environment.identifier` in the bundle's `manifest.json`. This new field allows the content to target a specific execution environment when running on Connect. The existing `environment.image` field remains unchanged however the semantics are slightly different. An `image` selection is now treated the same as any other piece of matching criteria. Connect will choose _any_ execution environment that uses the specified container image. 

We should add an `environment_id` flag to both `deployApp` and `writeManifest` - the value is the guid of the target execution environment in Connect and it should be written to `environment.identifier` in the manifest.json.

We should also add arguments the following arguments to `deployApp`: `default_image` and `default_environment_id`. These arguments accepts an image name and an execution environment guid respectively, however instead of writing these to the manfiest.json, we should update the App record in Connect to set the `app.default_image_name` and `app.default_environment_guid` fields. This new workflow allows users to call `deployApp(..., default_image='my/custom/image:latest')` or `deployApp(..., default_environment_id='<env-guid>')` only once and the image/environment will continue to be used for subsequent deployments (as long as it isn't overwritten by another deployment). This means that the arguments doesn't need to be provided everytime `deployApp(...)` is called which is how the current `image` argument behaves. This is the same workflow used by the Connect dashboard.

title: Using reticulate with uv python
description:
Reticulate v1.41 added a new feature where reticulate will automatically generate ephemeral virtual environments based on R session requirements. 

This feature works on Connect, but rsconnect is not yet aware of this feature, and will throw an error if an app uses reticulate but a manually-configured reticulate-python is not discovered.

For now, it's straightforward to workaround by setting this option before deploying

```r
options(rsconnect.python.enabled = FALSE)
```

However, it would be nice if rsconnect would automatically "do nothing" w.r.t. python discovery if reticulate will default to using an ephemeral reticulate-uv managed python.

One way to detect if reticulate will use an ephemeral uv venv is by checking `is.null(reticulate::py_discover_config())` before reticulate has initialized python.

Additionally, one way users can force reticulate to use an ephemeral uv env is by setting `RETICULATE_PYTHON="managed"`. Any checking of envvar `RETICULATE_PYTHON` should to be updated to accommodate the value "managed".

title: `rsconnect` doesn't correctly detect if it's publishing a single file, or a directory for `recordDir` location
description:
Apparently, `rsconnect` incorrectly determines whether your project/Shiny application is a directory vs a file based on the R package `tools::file_ext() ` here solely based on the existence of any "extension". The issue is that a naming convention of `framework.appname`, ex: `shiny.awesomeapp`. Since `rsconnect` is only checking for the existence of an extension, the `recordDir /rsconnect` is being placed in the parent directory of their application rather than alongside the application in their `workingDir`. This results in two negative outcomes, 

1. They are put in the strange position of needing to copy this file manually into their `shiny.awesomeapp` directory in order to keep the `shiny.dcf` and their application together in version control. 
2.  It results in any future collaborators who clone their repository needing to copy this directory out of `shiny.awesomeapp` one level higher in the directory structure in order to republish the application. Additionally, the Publish button in RStudio doesn't show Republish when the `rsconnect` directory is in the current working directory of `shiny.awesomeapp` .

The fix to this issue may be as simple as changing the logic here:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/a3ebf70adb96a020fb8844b7194870ae04500a1d/R/config.R#L134

```
#Current Logic: 
> isDocumentPath <- function(path) {
+   tools::file_ext(path) != ""
+ }
> isDocumentPath("/home/sam.cofer/shiny.test")
[1] TRUE
> deploymentConfigDir("/home/sam.cofer/shiny.test")
[1] "/home/sam.cofer/rsconnect/documents/shiny.test"
> isDocumentPath <- function(path) {
+   !fs::is_dir(path)
+ }
> isDocumentPath("/home/sam.cofer/shiny.test")
/home/sam.cofer/shiny.test 
                     FALSE 
> deploymentConfigDir("/home/sam.cofer/shiny.test")
[1] "/home/sam.cofer/shiny.test/rsconnect"
```

With this example, we can see that this change correctly identifies this directory as a directory, rather than a file. I'm not sure if there are any other downstream repercussions, but this change seems like it would better align with how client OS's detect files.

title: renv and private GitLab packages
description:
Hi rsconnect team,
 
I am having an issue with deploying an R shiny app to RStudio Connect. I am using renv for managing the packages, which include a mix of sources like CRAN, public Github repos and a self-hosted GitLab repo. The latter is where problems arise.
 
I can install these packages in R without issues – either by downloading a local tar.gz and installing from source or by generating a PAT in GitLab and following the answer here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62772833/use-renv-for-private-gitlab-package. If I install from source, it is easy for my colleagues to update their local renv as well.
 
However, when I want to deploy the package, I run into a series of issues. With local sourced packages, I cannot write the manifest:

```
Error in `createAppManifest()` at rsconnect/R/deployApp.R:648:2:
! All packages must be installed from a reproducible location.
✖ Can't re-install packages installed from source: <package>.
``` 

With packages from our in-house GitLab, I get the following messages during install:

```
Installing <package> (<version>) ...
curl: HTTP 404 <address_of_repo>//api/v4/projects/<package1>%2F<package2>/repository/archive?sha=<sha>
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
…
FAILED
Error in value[[3L]](cond): Failed to download package from URL:
- <address_of_repo>//api/v4/projects/<package1>%2F<package2>/repository/archive?sha=<sha>'
- Reason: Error in doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler): Download failure.
```

I am using R 4.2.0, rsconnect 1.3.4 and renv 1.0.11.
 
I came across the issue [Packrat unable to restore package from private Gitlab · Issue #625 · rstudio/packrat](https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/issues/625), but that seems to have been related to a required update to allow gitlab as a source. I have also been reading on [R Package Management – Posit Connect Documentation Version 2024.12.0](https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/r/package-management/#configuring-on-posit-connect), but I didn’t find any solutions that worked – and I don’t have the rights to modify the `/etc/rstudio-connect/rstudio-connect.gcfg` file.
 
Any help would be greatly appreciated.
 
Thanks,
Christina

title: Deployment fails with lock file in custom location
description:
I am running a `shiny` app in an R project, let's call it the _parent app_. The project has a `renv.lock` file but it is not located in the project root. The file's location is defined in the environment variable `RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE`, which is set in the `.Rprofile` of the project, before `renv/activate.R` is run. So far, so good.

The parent app generates code for another `shiny` app, let's call this one the _daughter app_. The daughter app file is placed in a separate directory in within the project. From there the daughter app is deployed while the parent app is running.

This process fails because the lock file is not found. It does work when the lock file is located in the project root (as usual) or when it is copied from the location specified by the env var to the project root before calling `deployApp`. Note that there is no attempt at creating a lock file - it is not found where expected and an error is raised.

Can this be fixed so that custom location of the lock file is taken into account?

data/unfiltered/dataset_1.rds
data/unfiltered/dataset_2.rds
```

I did some testing and it looks like anything with a subfolder path doesn't work. I could remove a level (making the `filtered` and `unfiltered` folders both root-level), but would be nice for organization's sake to have the `.rscignore` recognize paths like this.

title: writeManifest lexical error - too long chunk
description:
When creating manifest:
`writeManifest(appFiles = 'test1.qmd')` we got error:
```
Error: lexical error: invalid character inside string.
          st_test\n### test_test_test_te st_test_test_test_test_test_t
                     (right here) ------^
```
trying to pinpoint the issue we came to line where `quarto.exe inspect` is called:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/848b15fc273ad99c9d851628a6e1974293058e10/R/appMetadata-quarto.R#L48

Trying to split the chunk, resolves the issue.
Are there any character length limitation for single quarto chunk?
The dashboard works fine when chunks are large, so the problem only comes up when we need to create a manifest file for deployment to Posit Connect.

Example dashboard code:
[test1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17556120/test1.zip)

title: RSPM archived package (rgdal) cannot be resolved
description:
Given the following `Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM rstudio/r-base:4.0-jammy

RUN export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    && apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y \
    curl \
    libcurl4-openssl-dev \
    libgdal-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ARG REPO=https://cran.rstudio.com
# ARG REPO=https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest
RUN R -e "install.packages('shiny', repos=c(CRAN='${REPO}')); library(shiny)"

RUN R -e "install.packages('remotes', repos=c(CRAN='${REPO}')); library(remotes)"
RUN R -e "remotes::install_version('rgdal','1.6-7', repos=c(CRAN='${REPO}')); library(rgdal)"

RUN R -e "install.packages('rsconnect', repos=c(CRAN='${REPO}')); library(rsconnect)"

COPY app.R /content/app.R

WORKDIR /content

RUN R -e "options(repos=c(CRAN='${REPO}/',RSPM='${REPO}')); rsconnect::appDependencies()" > dependencies.txt
RUN R -e "options(repos=c(CRAN='${REPO}/',RSPM='${REPO}')); rsconnect::writeManifest()"
```

and a very simple `app.R`:

```r
library(shiny)
library(rgdal)

ui <- fluidPage("hello")
server <- function(input, output) {}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Dependencies can be resolved from CRAN, but not from RSPM.

```bash
# succeeds
docker build -t shiny-rgdal .

# fails
docker build --build-arg REPO=https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest -t shiny-rgdal-p3m .
```

The error message:

```
0.519 > options(repos=c(CRAN='https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest/',RSPM='https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest')); rsconnect::writeManifest()
0.647 ℹ Capturing R dependencies with renv
11.65 ✔ Found 33 dependencies
11.75 Error in `createAppManifest()`:
11.75 ! All packages must be installed from a reproducible location.
11.75 ✖ Can't re-install packages installed from source: rgdal.
11.75 ℹ See `rsconnect::appDependencies()` for more details.
11.75 Backtrace:
11.75     ▆
11.75  1. └─rsconnect::writeManifest()
11.75  2.   └─rsconnect:::createAppManifest(...)
11.75  3.     └─rsconnect:::bundlePackages(...)
11.75  4.       └─rsconnect:::checkBundlePackages(deps, call = error_call)
11.75  5.         └─cli::cli_abort(...)
11.75  6.           └─rlang::abort(...)
11.76 Execution halted
```

This is caused by an inability to associate the `rgdal` package to a repository.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/666bb3753f185c4b186943a0c6fc54b72ab0b079/R/bundlePackageRenv.R#L99-L113

This code handles "CRAN" differently from "RSPM". The calls to `findRepoUrl()` and `findRepoName()` both produce NA.

title: discover DESCRIPTIONS without a populated library
description:
Some ideas from @kevinushey:

1. Use `crandb`, e.g. https://crandb.r-pkg.org/dplyr/1.0.0. The JSON might need to be transformed into a more DESCRIPTION-like shape before it is shoved into the manifest. We might have whitespace differences, but not in a way that matters for package hashing.
2. Extract the DESCRIPTION files from the repos beneath https://github.com/cran.

Neither of these suggestions help with packages containing Git references. We might be better off understanding what information is needed by rsconnect + (Connect+shinyapps.io) and make sure that is available in the renv.lock.

title: App Fails on Redeployment at shinyapps.io
description:
I have a shinyapps.io app that is working well (https://solo-fsw.shinyapps.io/lavaangui/). I made some updates and locally the new app is working well. However, it does not work on shinyapps.io. After some troubleshooting, I testing downloading the bundle from the working app (https://solo-fsw.shinyapps.io/lavaangui/) and reploying without any changes (to https://solo-fsw.shinyapps.io/lavaanguitest/). The redeployed app does also not work on shinyapps.io, even though, the R code of the working and not working app is 100% the same. There are slight differences in manifest.json but it was not obvious to me how these should break my app. 

**Details**
The steps that work at https://solo-fsw.shinyapps.io/lavaangui/ and not at https://solo-fsw.shinyapps.io/lavaanguitest/ are File-->Load Model and Data and then select the file contained in this zip archive:[cfa.lvd.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17289941/cfa.lvd.zip). Then select Estimates in the bottom toolbar. The bundles are here: [bundles.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17289970/bundles.zip). 
I deployed the new app like this:

rsconnect::deployApp(
  appName = "lavaanguitest",

  appFiles = c(

    "R/",
    "inst/",
    "NAMESPACE",
    "DESCRIPTION",
    "app.R"
  ),
  appId = rsconnect::deployments(".")$appID,

)

title: writeManifest fails if using renv profiles
description:
If you are using the profiles feature of renv then the lockfile doesn't get written to the location expected by `writeManifest()` and the function fails with a cryptic error.

Optimally, `renvLockFile()` needs to be a bit smarter and find lockfiles related to the current profile

title: Multiple accounts created for one account
description:
I realize this is hard to reproduce. :( I tried to deploy the example stock app from RStudio a couple of times, stopped the deployment after ~15 minutes, it was stuck at determining session server location, then tried to call `rsconnect::deployApp()` from the console, that's stuck as well.

Now I have a state where seemingly I have multiple deployments:
```

Is this expected? Maybe rsconnect could detect that these are the same and offer some advice?

title: checkAppLayout() fails when app.R is present even if app.R not included in appFiles
description:
This was mostly an accidental edge case but when working in a directory with multiple single-file Shiny apps, one of which happened to be named `app.R`, it was no longer possible to deploy the other apps even when `app.R` was not selected as part of the deployment. 

This occurs both with the RStudio gui or with the direct package interface:

```r
rsconnect::deployApp(appFiles = "shiny.R", appPrimaryDoc = "shiny.R")
## ── Preparing for deployment ─────────────────────────────
## ✔ Deploying "shiny" to "server: rstudio02-metaproxy.production05.posit.academy / username: rundel@gmail.com"
## Error in `checkAppLayout()`:
## ! Project must not contain both app.R and a single-file Shiny app.
## Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

What I was trying to do is clearly not advisable but still seems undesirable that it should trigger an error and prevent deployment without renaming or moving files.

title: `deployApp` should fail if the app contains `deployApp`
description: Similar to #100 this is a common problem when novice users try and deploy apps and come looking for help on Stack Overflow. There is no reason why you would ever want to do this, so it would seem sensible to prevent it as early as possible. I'm happy to submit a PR to address this and #100 if there is consensus it would be sensible to do so.

title: `writeManifest()` gives confusing error if no `app.R`
description:
i.e. create a new project with file `foo.R` containing `library(shiny)`, then run `writeManfiest()`:

Error in `quartoInspect()`:
! Failed to run `quarto inspect` against your content:
ERROR: /Users/hadleywickham/Desktop/madlibs2/madlibs.R is not a valid
Quarto input document
```

Presumably because it's using the wrong primary document, but why is it passing an R file to quarto? Should also log about the primary file.

title: `deployApp()` should throw a warning if `appMode` is inferred to be static
description:
Someone who calls `deployApp()` is expecting to deploy an interactive application, but `deployApp()` might incorrectly infer the application is static. As a user, I picked `deployApp()` over `deployDoc()` because I wanted to deploy an __application__.

```
> quarto::quarto_publish_app(
+   "dashboard.qmd",
+   name = "app-name",
+   server = "connect.example.com"
+ )
── Preparing for deployment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✔ Deploying "app-name" using "server: connect.example.com / username: gadenbuie"
ℹ Creating application on server...
✔ Created application with id 10
✔ Created 911,909b bundle
ℹ Uploading bundle...
✔ Uploaded bundle with id 13
── Deploying to server ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Building static content...
Launching static content...
── Deployment complete ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✔ Successfully deployed to https://connect.example.com/content/4c3ede83-2870-4f1b-bf20-ca2aa8c51714/
```

When this happens, it's not immediately clear how to fix it and I think many people, myself included, will look for problems in the source document rather than investigating arguments to `deployApp()`.

The solution is to explicitly set `appMode` to one of `"shiny"`, `"rmd-shiny", or `"quarto-shiny"` -- or even `"static"` if a static application is truly desired. A warning message could easily instruct the user how to make this change.

description:
`rsconnect::writeManifest()` fails when the target directory contains a *.qmd file

The output is:

title: provide more execution context to rsconnect deployment hooks
description:
These hooks has limited knowledge of its execution context.  Specifically, I understand from reading [rsconnectOptions](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/rsconnect/html/options.html) documentation and the [source code]() that functions named by these options are called with a single argument, being the appDir.

I would like my rsconnect.post.deploy hook function to somehow determine more of the execution context, specifically the path to the deployment record (.dcf) file.

Can this be made possible somehow?

I have also raised this issue [in posit a forum post](https://forum.posit.co/t/rsconnect-deployment-hooks-guidance/188900) and with Posit support, who advised me that this would make a good feature request here.

title: How do I deploy an ‘renv’ app from inside a *different* project?
description:
I am trying to deploy a Plumber API that is using ‘renv’ via `rsconnect::deployApp()`. I am calling `deployApp()` from *outside* that project because I don’t want to add the ‘rsconnect’ package as a dependency to my project (I want to keep its dependencies as lean as possible).

Unfortunately this fails since the packages inside the Plumber API renv have different versions than the ones outside the project:

```r
rsconnect::deployApp('plumber-api', appId = app_id, acocunt = account, server = server)
```

> ```
> ── Preparing for deployment ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> […]
> ℹ Capturing R dependencies from renv.lock
> Error in `parseRenvDependencies()`:
> ! Library and lockfile are out of sync
> ℹ Use renv::restore() or renv::snapshot() to synchronise
> ℹ Or ignore the lockfile by adding to your .rscignore
> Backtrace:
>     ▆
>  1. └─rsconnect (local) deployApp(dir, appId = app_id, account = "default", server = "default")
>  2.   └─rsconnect:::bundleApp(...)
>  3.     └─rsconnect:::createAppManifest(...)
>  4.       └─rsconnect:::bundlePackages(...)
>  5.         └─rsconnect:::computePackageDependencies(...)
>  6.           └─rsconnect:::parseRenvDependencies(bundleDir)
>  7.             └─cli::cli_abort(...)
>  8.               └─rlang::abort(...)
> ```

And indeed I can recapitulate this by looking at the package versions between my `plumber-api` project and the currently active project.

I also tried activating the `plumber-api` renv project before calling `deployApp()` via `renv::load('plumber-api')` but that doesn’t solve the issue, since `parseRenvDependencies()` internally calls `packageDescription(…, lib.loc = NULL)` to find the installed package version; however, for packages that are already loaded this will read the *loaded package’s* package description, not the ones from the suitable renv library.

Keeping the dependencies between these two projects in sync would be a non-trivial effort.

I believe the fix would be to replace

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/9999fdb11dde6d5efe596677f9a6be6bd779e31d/R/bundlePackageRenv.R#L51

with

```r
  deps$description <- lapply(deps$Package, package_record, lib_dir = renv::paths$library(project = bundleDir))
```

I’m happy to create a PR but I don’t really know how to create a good, self-contained test case for that — I’d have to create a mock package and install two different versions of that in two different projects.

title: Add to manifest when deploying a golem shiny app on connect
description:
This is more a feature idea that I don't know if it is possible.

If I understand things correctly, when I want to deploy a Shiny app that is written with Golem, from GitHub on Posit connect, the manifest file has to have the app as part of packages that need to be installed. This requires to install the app in the local environment with `remotes::install_github()` and then to `rsconnect::writeManifest()`. However, updating the manifest without having the app in the environment, removes the app from the manifest, and then the deployment is non-functional.

It seems like a good idea to have the option to say something like `rsconnect::addToManifest()` and then list the GitHub dependency, instead of having to remember to have it in the environment each time the manifest is rewritten.

title: Setting environment variable does not work
description:
I'm trying to deploy a shiny app to Shinyapps.io using rsconnect-python and the following command:

`rsconnect deploy shiny path/to/my/app --name my-acount-name --title my-app-name --environment OPENAI_API_KEY='my key'`

Here, `path/to/my/app` is the directory that contains (1) an `app.py` script that makes use of OPENAI_API_KEY to call GPT models and (2) a `requirements.txt` file containing the dependency. Locally, everything runs correctly. But when I push to Shinyapps.io, the app does not work with error message telling me that the OpenAI api key has not been set. 

Any advice would be much appreciated!

title: Cannot get Posit Connect to work with `manifest.json` generated by `rsconnect`
description:
First of all, thank you so much for your work on this awesome package! The firm I work at is using Posit Connect to deploy some apps and dashboards, and we need to use an internal package which implements the heavy-duty number crunching to power some of them. However, I cannot get seem to get our setup to work with the private repo containing this package. When publishing using the 'Git-backed content' option, I get the error 'package <internal-package> does not define Repository'.

I suspect the problem is related to the fact that I installed the package using `install_git` prior to calling `writeManifest`. In #640, the problem was resolved by changing this to `install_github`. However, that's not an option for us since we use a Bitbucket server with a private URL, which is not compatible with `install_bitbucket` (see r-lib/remotes#584). Any idea how I could resolve this?

title: Support for supplying image via environment variable
description:
`rsconnect` since version 0.8.26 supports specifying an image for the deployed content which is really great. 

It would be very helpful if `rsconnect` could not only explicitly use the `image` argument in the `rsconnect()` function call but also pick it up from an environment variable. 

The use case is that on a given environment a default image can be defined and - unless the user overwrites it by specifying the image in the `rsconnect()` call will use this one for publishing.

title: connectUser / connectApiUser: let server be a URL
description:
When `connectUser()` and `connectApiUser()` are provided a `server` value that is a URL rather than a `servers()` name, consider treating that value as a Connect URL and call `addServer()` to add a server entry.

```r
# existing use:
rsconnect::connectUser("alice", "connect")

# suggested enhancement:
rsconnect::connectUser("alice", "https://connect.company.com")
```

With this change, folks could add a new Connect account with a single call rather than the two that we require today.

title: addServer: Suggest connectUser() and connectApiUser() as next steps
description:

title: How to pre-install Python dependencies for reticulated project?
description:
Hi, 

I have successfully deployed a reticulated project with the following `app.R`, but when I include `tensorflow` in `py_install()`, the app will take too long to start up because of the installation and shinyapps.io will shut it down.

```r
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

reticulate::py_install(c("numpy", "Pillow"),
                       envname = "r-web_interface",
                       method = c("virtualenv"))
reticulate::use_virtualenv("r-web_interface")

PIL <- reticulate::import('PIL')
np <- reticulate::import("numpy")

server <- function(input, output) { 
  output$py_config <- renderText(capture.output(reticulate::py_config()))
}

ui <- fluidPage(textOutput('py_config'))

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

**Is there a way to pre-install all these Python dependencies at build time?**

It seems like there is a solution provided at https://solutions.posit.co/write-code/reticulate/, but when I deploy the app with the RStudio button, the published app will ignore all the Python dependencies (I have downloaded and checked the `manifest.json` file of the deployed app). 

And if I use `rsconnect::writeManifest()` first to generate `manifest.json` and `requirements.txt`, then deploy the app with the rsconnect cli - `rsconnect deploy manifest manifest.json`, the deployed app will not be able to find a Python interpreter at `.venv/bin/python`.

title: Runtime failure of deployed application from suggested package
description:
I recently encountered the following runtime failure of an application deployed to Connect:
* A Shiny app was using the `pins` package to read a pin stored on Connect.
* This pin had been created using the parquet format.
* Therefore the `arrow` package was needed to execute the code.
* However, the `arrow` package was never mentioned explicitly in the code and therefore not included in the manifest.

One workaround is to add `library(arrow)` explicitly to the Shiny app. And I am not sure if it is possible to detect such run-time dependencies at deployment time (that would be the ideal solution).   It would be helpful if the user could be informed about the fact that packages used in the application (i.e. part of the manifest) are suggesting some packages that seemingly are not used in the application (i.e. not in the manifest) but are installed in the local environment. I am undecided if this would be better during the deployment or as the result of a separate function call.

title: Add posibility of bypassing "Library and lockfile are out of sync" check.
description:
Hey 

With release of rsconnect 1.0.0 - i was really happy to learn that you could use a renv.lock file for specifying deployment dependencies. 

This was a big help since the release script in our azure pipelines, had different dependencies from the actual apps that we were deploying. This helped us sort these problems.  However with the functionality that enforce that the Library and lockfile can't be out of sync. We again have this problem. That is the deployment script need to have the same dependencies as specified in the app. 

I understand that the change was made  to avoid having different experiences locally and on the connect server. So therefore i would like to suggest that we might add an argument to deployApp and writeManifest that allows us to bypass the check.

title: appDependencies reliance on available.packages()
description: Perhaps this is a known phenomenon, but a search came up empty. The background is we have an internal Nexus repository which mirrors CRAN, but occasionally `available.packages()` doesn't reflect the latest package versions right away. For example, yesterday I was able to install `box` version `1.2.0` directly from Nexus, but running `available.packages()` said version `1.1.3`. I tried to deploy a shiny app, but encountered an error which led back to `rsconnect::appDependencies`. The problem seems to be that `rsconnect:::snapshotRenvDependencies` returns `NA` for the `Repository` field because it couldn't find box version `1.2.0` in the return from `available.packages()`. Though the root cause is likely in the Nexus space (a separate topic), perhaps the error message could be clarified that there is a problem with the repository reporting a stale version, as opposed to the package installation?

title: writeManifest does not work with renv profiles
description:
In [`computePackageDependencies`](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/ece7cfcf22995c385e980ad134d006b6268a881c/R/bundlePackage.R#L55) the check for whether an `renv.lock` file exists only checks for a file in the `bundleDir`. If you are using renv profiles the check returns FALSE, so it falls back to the case of trying to create a new renv lock file.

It would be nice if writeManifest could accept as an argument the name of an renv profile to use, or automatically detect the currently active renv profile.

Locally, I've monkey-patched `renvLockFile` to return the path to the profile in use in my specific project. This seems to work and successfully generates the `manifest.json` file for me

``` r
assignInNamespace(
  "renvLockFile",
  \(...) "renv/profiles/dev/renv.lock",
  "rsconnect"
)
```

title: Need multiple locales when deployed to shinyapps.io
description:
I've built an app where users have the option to generate reports in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. The reports have a time stamp at the top that relies on `Sys.setlocale` and `format` to translate and display the date properly depending on the selected language. (E.g. "02 março, 2023" for Portuguese.) Works locally, but not when deployed.

Stripped down app.R:
```
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(tools) # cap functions

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(
    inputId="langSel",
    label="Select Lanugage",
    choices=c("English"="en_US",
              "Spanish"="es_MX",
              "Portuguese"="pt_BR"),
    selected="en_US"
  ),
  textOutput("repDateOut")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  timeStamp <- "2023-03-02"
  
  # set locale depending on language selection to translate month
  observeEvent(input$langSel,{
    Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", paste0(input$langSel,".UTF-8"))
  })
  
  repDate <- reactive({
    dateOrder <- if (input$langSel=="en_US"){
      '%B %d, %Y' # month before day for English
    } else {
      '%d %B, %Y' # day before month for everything else
    }
    fmDate <- format(as.Date(timeStamp), dateOrder) %>%
      {if (input$langSel=="en_US") toTitleCase(.) else .} # cap month for English only
    fmDate
  })
  
  # print timestamp
  output$repDateOut <- renderText({repDate()})
  
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Following the advice [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66896516/set-locale-on-shinyapps-io-via-ghactions) about making non-local locales available in rsconnect before deploying, I've tried running a few things in the console to deploy the app:

Attempt 1:

```
options(rsconnect.locale.cache = FALSE, rsconnect.locale = "en_US.UTF-8")
options(rsconnect.locale.cache = FALSE, rsconnect.locale = "pt_BR.UTF-8")
options(rsconnect.locale.cache = FALSE, rsconnect.locale = "es_MX.UTF-8")
rsconnect::deployApp()
```

Attempt 2:

```
options(rsconnect.locale.cache = FALSE, rsconnect.locale = "en_US.UTF-8")
options(rsconnect.locale = "pt_BR.UTF-8")
options(rsconnect.locale = "es_MX.UTF-8")
rsconnect::deployApp()
```

Attempt 3:

```
options(rsconnect.locale.cache = FALSE, rsconnect.locale = "en_US.UTF-8", rsconnect.locale = "pt_BR.UTF-8", 
rsconnect.locale = "es_MX.UTF-8")
rsconnect::deployApp()
```

In each case, only the Spanish locale (last one specified) works, and I get the following errors in the log:

> OS reports request to set locale to "pt_BR.UTF-8" cannot be honored

> OS reports request to set locale to "en_US.UTF-8" cannot be honored

Is it possible to make all three available in shinyapps.io?

(Apologies for earlier crospostings [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77767273/use-multiple-locales-in-r-shinyapp-deployed-to-shinyapps-io) and [here](https://community.rstudio.com/t/use-multiple-locales-in-shinyapp-deployed-to-shinyapps-io/179892), but it didn't get any takers.)

title: quarto: provide feedback when inspect fails
description:
Given the Quarto document:

````markdown
---
format: unsupported
---

This is a Quarto document that attempts to use an unrecognized format.
````

Running `quarto inspect` produces an error.

```bash
quarto inspect index.qmd
# => ERROR: Unknown format unsupported
```

However, when `rsconnect::writeManifest()` or `rsconnect:deployApp()` acts upon this file, there is no complaint.

```r
rsconnect::writeManifest()
```

The manifest declares that it should be `quarto-static` but is created without a `quarto` block. Additionally, a set of R packages is inferred, as if it needs knitr/rmarkdown.

When `rsconnect::deployApp()` publishes to Posit Connect, the lack of a Quarto block produces an error:

```
── Deployment complete ───
✖ Deployment failed with error: Unsupported App Mode.
```

This type of error can happen when the document uses a new type of format but the Quarto installation does not support that format.

title: Connect accounts registered with rsconnect 0.8.29 cannot deploy to new locations with current rsconnect
description:
User registration previously recorded `username` in the account DCF file.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/9ce427edf03b6d243a4074264dbc950242b0a295/R/accounts.R#L409-L439

We now record `name`.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/98ccc9ae05bec7d49b38f1d10d0be5b48d03fda7/R/accounts.R#L325-L358

The `accountInfo` function does not rewrite `username` to `name`, which can cause problems for downstream code that expects account records to contain a stable set of fields.
