Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 1245073364 failed: Error building image: R version 4.2.2 currently unavailable
```

It was fixed by downgrading the deployment version to 4.2.1.

It appears that the latest R version 4.2.2 is not supported on shinyapps. Is there an estimated time window between R version releases and when users may expect to have version support on shinyapps.io and for shiny apps in general? Going forward, I would like to make sure that any automatic deployments are not affected by new version delays.

title: ignore project-local python virtual environments by default
description:
An internal user encountered the following while attempting to deploy a reticulated project:

```
Error in enforceBundleLimits(appDir, files$totalSize, length(files$contents)) : 
  The directory /usr/home/jeremy.allen/projects/reticulate-with-venv cannot be deployed because it contains too many files (the maximum number of files is 10000). Remove some files or adjust the rsconnect.max.bundle.files option.`
```

you can work around this by adjusting the max bundle files or by specifying `appFiles` but ignoring the files to begin with might be a better default.

title: Need better support for private repositories
description:
When using a private package repository that requires authentication, some users store their credentials in `~/.Rprofile` and others store credentials by adding the private package repo directly in the IDE via `Settings > Packages > Management`. When creating a `manifest.json` with `rsconnect::writeManifest()`, the `Repository` field includes the credentials that are used to connect to the private repository.

```
https://{{USER}}:{{TOKEN}}@cran.myorg.com
```

This is a blocker for publishers who wish to perform git-backed deployments using a private package repository that requires authentication because the repo credentials would be committed to source control.

title: We do not need to specify contentCategory in deployApp
description:
This was removed with https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/304.  

Unfortunately, it returned with the fix to https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/204 (https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/commit/9e768e87c9a63885f175ccbc4ed69eb6c503f0f2; no PR?)

This check is happening ahead of the call to bundleApp, which means that we have not yet determined the appMode.  This issue was raised as part of https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/621 but was deemed to be too large of a refactor, thus creating this separate issue.

title: publishing credentials files with a + in the name are not usable
description:
If i created a publishing credential with a `+` in the filename, the file cannot be found when trying to use it.

```
> rsconnect::deployApp("myapp")
Error in accountInfo(accounts) : 
  account named 'myemail+test@rstudio.com' does not exist
```

Pretty sure its because of this code:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/8c98105575c4823606db93a5aa23944765529dcc/R/accounts.R#L441-L451

`list-files` treats `pattern` as a regular expression where + has special meaning. If the + is double escaped, then it would find the file.

title: We should remove the API check for plumber APIs when deploying to cloud or shinyapps.io.
description:
There's validation on the content type when the bundle is uploaded now - so we can remove this check,

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/main/R/deployApp.R#L339-L346

title: How to find which R package version should be used for shiny server deployment?
description:
I just started to use rsconnect in my company, and tried to deploy a shiny app from my windows machine. The server comes with R 4.1.0, and one of the packages requires to install `terra`.

I have tried multiple R package repos from Rstudio dev-cran with different dates to install `terra`, and tried version 1.2-10, 1.3-4, ... all the way to the latest version. 

However, none of them was able to be uploaded, or installed during deployment. 
For the versions before 1.4, the error was

```
Uploading bundle for application: 335...Error: node stack overflow
Execution halted
```
while for versions above 1.4, parts of the error were

```
The requested URL returned error: 407
RStudio Connect cannot download a package because the R package repository (for example, CRAN or RStudio Package Manager) cannot be accessed.

```
This happened to other packages too, but the issue was usually resolved after I uninstalled and re-installed with a different repo. But for `terra`, I was not able to find a repo to fix the issue.  

Any suggestions for the next step?

title: FR: .rsconnect_profile file for the server
description:
Hello,

I need to execute some code on the server before the deployment. With the **.rsconnect_profile** file, the code is executed on my computer, not on the server. Therefore I use the **.Rprofile** file. But then I have to use a if-else in this file, to execute some code on my laptop and some code on the server. To be clearer, my **.Rprofile** file has form:

```r
os <- Sys.info()["sysname"]
if(os == "Windows") { # this is my computer
  ......
} else { # this is the RSconnect server
  ......
}
```

This is not highly convenient. It would be nice to have a file like **.rsconnect_profile** but whose contents are executed on the server.

title: "File paths are case-sensitive on deployment server" error when deploying to shinyapps.io
description: ### System details RStudio Edition : Desktop RStudio Version : 2022.7.1.554 OS Version : aarch64-apple-darwin20 (64-bit) macOS Monterey 12.5 R Version : 4.2.1 (2022-06-23) ### Steps to reproduce the problem When deploying shiny app to shinyapps.io, an error for review comes up. It appears to arise from the following line: ``` tidyr::separate(value, into = c("description", "value"), sep = ":|=", extra = "merge") ``` Including this line in an R script for an app deployed to shinyapps.io reproduces the issue for me. As best I can tell, its the inclusion of the word "description" in the into argument. removing description appears to fix the issue for me. ### Describe the problem in detail ### Describe the behavior you expected As far as I can tell, this is not an error. Apologies if I'm mistaken or have missed a previous report of this issue. - [x] I have read the guide for [submitting good bug reports](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports). - [x] I have installed the latest version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists. - [x] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200321257-Running-a-Diagnostics-Report). - [x] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.

title: API Key Workflow and Server Registration should have better diagnostics
description:
Server registration right now is fairly naive and the happy path is pretty narrow. Even savvy users can get tripped up by this.

In particular, you _must_ have `/__api__` _with no trailing slash_ in order to have a functional server definition.

- To reproduce a 404 issue (missing `__api__` in server URL):
```
rsconnect::addServer("https://myserver.com", "training")
# Server 'training' added successfully: https://myserver.com
rsconnect::connectApiUser("cole", "training", "mykey")
# Account registered successfully: cole
rsconnect::deployApp("./test-123/", server = "training", account = "cole")
# Preparing to deploy application...Error: HTTP 404
# GET https://myserver.com/applications?filter=account_id:2&filter=name:test-123&count=100&offset=0
# 404 page not found
```
- To reproduce a different error (trailing slash)
```
rsconnect::addServer("https://myserver.com/__api__/", "training")
# Server 'training' added successfully: https://myserver.com/__api__/
rsconnect::deployApp("./test-123/", server = "training", account = "cole")
# Preparing to deploy application...Error in response[[listName]] : subscript out of bounds
```
- Success (no trailing slash)
```
rsconnect::addServer("https://myserver.com/__api__", "training")
# Server 'training' added successfully: https://myserver.com/__api__
rsconnect::deployApp("./test-123/", server = "training", account = "cole")
# Preparing to deploy application...DONE
# Uploading bundle for application: 56...DONE
# Deploying bundle: 59 for application: 56 ...
# ...
```

title: rsconnect: infer Quarto info for document deployments where `appPrimaryDoc` is not specified
description:
Currently, when calling `deployApp()` and `writeManifest()`, you can deploy R Markdown documents with a `quarto-static` or `quarto-shiny` app mode. However, to do this, you must explicitly pass `appPrimaryDoc`.

This discussion started in a previous PR: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/595#issuecomment-1169110104.

The difficulty in solving this that if it is not specified explicitly, the `appPrimaryDoc` is inferred _after_ the app mode is inferred, and uses the app mode to gate its functionality.

The proposed involves adding a new fallback heuristic to `inferQuartoInfo()`. If we don't have Quarto info after attempting `quarto inspect` on the directory and the explicitly-provided `appPrimaryDoc`, we can run `inferAppPrimaryDoc()` within `inferQuartoInfo()`, passing in a fake `quarto-static` app mode to make sure the function runs, and attempt to run `quarto inspect` on the resulting hypothetical `appPrimaryDoc`.

title: typo: rscignore vs rcsignore
description:
Present in both `NEWS.md` and [`R/deployApp.R`](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/main/R/deployApp.R#L12).

```
#' @param appFiles The files and directories to bundle and deploy (only if
#'   `upload = TRUE`). Can be `NULL`, in which case all the files in the
#'   directory containing the application are bundled, with the exception of
#'   any listed in an `.rcsignore` file. Takes precedence over
#'   `appFileManifest` if both are supplied.
```

It reads ``` `.rcsignore` ``` and should read ``` `.rscignore` ```.

title: rsconnect: disallow deployment of qmd files as R Markdown
description:
Currently, `.qmd` files will be deployed as R Markdown content if no `quarto` argument is passed to `deployApp()`, and an R Markdown manifest will be created if no `quarto` is passed to `writeManifest()`.

This is because Quarto files and R Markdown files are detected [with the same regular expression](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/27c50cb1be28a05ad2a62682e867515580ab1691/R/bundle.R#L410), and the `quarto` argument determines the app mode assigned.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/27c50cb1be28a05ad2a62682e867515580ab1691/R/bundle.R#L413-L420

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/27c50cb1be28a05ad2a62682e867515580ab1691/R/bundle.R#L430-L437

To change this, we should add a separate regex to detect `qmdFiles`. If `rmdFiles > `, the deployment will receive an `rmd`-related app mode. Otherwise, it will receive a `qmd`-related app mode.

Our reasoning in leaving this the other way was to make the selection of Quarto-related app modes manual, by passing in the `quarto` argument, which is a path to a Quarto binary. If the user does not pass that in, we won’t deploy as Quarto.

It almost seems silly to ask them to pass in a Quarto argument explicitly when we could just run `quarto inspect`. But I guess, they could get the same behavior by passing in `”quarto”` to that argument, because I don’t think we require a full path.

title: Any GitHub package present in a manifest adds `null`-valued `GitHub*` values to all packages in the manifest
description:
I came across while running some smoke tests, described in https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/pull/656#issuecomment-1035221766.

In that instance, the presence of the `emo` package in the dependencies added the following fields to all other packages in the manifest.

```
      "GithubRepo": null,
      "GithubUsername": null,
      "GithubRef": null,
      "GithubSha1": null,
```

For packages installed from GitHub, these fields contain relevant information that Connect uses when restoring the environment. For other packages, they're meaningless.
This probably isn't cause for too much concern, because this have almost certainly always been there, but it might be worth removing them.

@aronatkins [suspects](https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/pull/656#issuecomment-1035284712) it is due to a data frame being serialized to JSON.

title: Is is possible to deploy a shiny app object "shiny.appobj."
description:
Hi there,

is it possible to deploy a shiny app object with `rsconnect` on `shinyapps.io`?

I would image something like this, but this does (of course) not work since the argument appDir `must be a single element character vector`
```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  "Hello, world!"
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
}
app <- shinyApp(ui, server)

rsconnect::deployApp(app)
```

Thank you for your support,
Christian

title: deployment fails for projects using packages without known Source
description:
Not yet sure of the underlying cause, but a customer saw this issue during a deployment:

```
Error in if (isSCMSource(source)) { : argument is of length zero
Calls: <Anonymous> ... createAppManifest -> snapshotDependencies -> lapply -> FUN
In addition: Warning message:
Unable to package DESCRIPTION files: subscript out of bounds
Execution halted
```

The error most likely implies that `isSCMSource(source)` returned a length-zero vector; `source` is most likely `NULL`.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/e42166e4d0d39ead451165c30a0dd847dc11e639/R/dependencies.R#L159-L164

We should see if we can understand why the value could be `NULL` here.

title: Do not ignore the `renv` folder by default
description:
Note: I'm not sure if it's a `{rsconnect}` or `{renv}` issue, @kevinushey feel free to correct me if you think this feature should be in `{renv}` instead.

If I create a new `{shiny}` app, use `renv::init()`, then do `rsconnect::deployApp()`, it will fail. 

The reason behind this is that the .Rprofile contains a call to `source("renv/activate.R")`, and by default, clicking on the blue button in RStudio sends all the files except `renv/` & `renv.lock` (so does `rsconnect::deployApp()`. 

Also, trying to include the `renv/` folder by hand will fail: 

```r
> rsconnect::deployApp(appFiles = c("app.R", "renv/", "renv.lock", ".Rprofile"))
The following potential problems were identified in the project files:

The following lines contain calls to the browseURL function:
72: | `file_show("path")`                         | `browseURL("path")`               | `open path`                       |

The following lines contain calls to the browseURL function:
58: browseURL("http://localhost:9454/")

Remove browseURL calls; browseURL does not work in deployed applications.
Do you want to proceed with deployment? [Y/n]: Y
Preparing to deploy application...
Update application currently deployed at
https://colinfay.shinyapps.io/renvtest/? [Y/n] Y
DONE
Uploading bundle for application: 4258497...Error: Unable to retrieve package records for the following packages:
- 'foo', 'testRcppClass', 'testRcppInterfaceExporter', 'testRcppInterfaceUser', 'testRcppModule'
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
```

Possible solution : 

- From the user perspective : 
    - don't send the .RProfile, but that file is useful for other purposes, and  for example it's suggested to use this file here https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/1.5.4/admin/package-management.html#private-repositories
    - Comment in the .RProfile, but that means that you need to do this manually, and prevents from using an automatic deployment from git
    -  wrap the `source("renv/activate.R")` inside an if statement detecting if we are on Connect / shinyapps.io

- in `{rsconnect}` 
    - Deploy the `renv/` folder alongside the app 
    - Comment the .RProfile if it detects a `source("renv/activate.R")`

- in `{renv}`
	- always wrap the `source("renv/activate.R")` inside an if statement detecting if we are on Connect / shinyapps.io

That being said, maybe you have a better workflow here. 

I'm deploying apps on Connect from Git, that we locally build using `{renv}`, and that would be nice to have them both work flawlessly without tweaking the `.Rprofile` :) 

Cheers, 
Colin

title: rsconnect/packrat writeManifest - mechanism to exclude R specific packages
description:
We've recently seen some issues where rsconnect `writeManifest` has somehow pulled in the `credentials` package into the `manifest.json` file.

This is possibly via a path of `devtools` to `gert` to `credentials` somehow being included (I'm still looking to try to work out what is happening).

The result of this is that deployments to RStudio Connect fail - as the credentials package tries to access git config information which is beyond its security permissions (which is good).

I'd like to try to find some way to exclude this R package. 

I don't mind if this is in the writeManifest step or on the server in the deployment step - e.g. I discovered recently with the Python there's a way (on the server at least) to ignore packages (https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/#Python.ProhibitedPackage). 

I appreciate this is a bit vague as a feature request/question - hope it's ok to log this as an issue.

title: Faster deployments?
description:
Currently building a new instance of RSC into our workflows and we're finding first deployments take hours and subsequent deployments are still slow imo - easy around 20 minutes even when using cached packages.

So why is deploying apps to RSC so slow compared to other deploying containers to other containerised environments? and How can we make it faster? (both inside RSC, and speeding up the deployment through RSC configuration)

title: Packages in funny places aren't captured
description:
Two cases where required packages aren't captured:
1) If the package is only used to set default arguments in function definitions.
2) If the package is only used inside a `glue` string.

Neither the `here` nor the `scales` packages are captured for the code below:
```
my_fn <- function(x = here::here) {
   x
}

glue::glue("{scales::dollar(100)")
````

I've tar-ed and attached a project with this code and a working `renv` environment, so the code runs interactively, but dependencies aren't captured by `rsconnect` (probably actually `packrat`?).

[rstudio-export.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/files/6259895/rstudio-export.zip)

title: CRAN says rsconnect and reverse dependencies will be archived soon
description:
I received the following email from CRAN because the shinystan package I maintain uses `rsconnect::deployApp()`: 

> We have repeatedly asked for an update making package rsconnect comply
> with the CRAN Policy, with no reply from the maintainer thus far.
> 
> Thus, package rsconnect is now scheduled for archival on 2021-04-12,
> and archiving this will necessitate also archiving its strong reverse
> dependencies.
> 
> Please negotiate the necessary actions.

Are you planning on submitting a version of rsconnect that complies with CRAN policies before the deadline? If not I will have to modify my package to not use rsconnect, which is ok but I would rather not do that if you plan of fixing rsconnect. Please advise, thanks!

title: Python requirements.txt file on Windows includes local file paths
description:
I'm using python inside connect for the first time this week - so apologies if these are "newbie" errors.

I'm working on Windows desktop and discovering that the generated pip requirements.txt file includes some nasty local file paths which cause pip on the server to fail.

For example, using a standard notebook like https://github.com/sol-eng/python-examples/tree/master/rmarkdown-notebook

This causes `rsconnect::writeManifest("reticulate", "FirstAttempt.Rmd")` to generate a `requirements.txt` file:

```
certifi==2020.12.5
numpy @ file:///D:/bld/numpy_1610324703282/work
pandas @ file:///D:/bld/pandas_1607423921518/work
python-dateutil==2.8.1
pytz @ file:///home/conda/feedstock_root/build_artifacts/pytz_1612179539967/work
six @ file:///home/conda/feedstock_root/build_artifacts/six_1590081179328/work
wincertstore==0.2
```

This will not upload to the server unless I manually edit it down to:

```
certifi==2020.12.5
numpy
pandas
python-dateutil==2.8.1
pytz
six
wincertstore==0.2
```

I think this is somehow related to https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8174 - it seems like the miniconda distribution that RStudio installed has `pip --version` of `pip 21.0.1`

Is this just a bug in pip? Or is it something rsconnect needs to be aware of too?

title: PyPI repository not recorded in manifest
description:
If Python content uses a specific PyPI repository in order to get access to packages not available in default repositories, it is unlikely to work when published since that repository is not recorded in the manifest generated by rsconnect. You must instead manually ensure that the PyPI repository used by RStudio Connect has the packages your Python content requires. 

This is about to become a much more prevalent issue now that RStudio Package Manager allows you to create snapshots, which get their own repository URLs. 

https://solo.rstudiopm.com/client/#/repos/32/overview

https://docs.rstudio.com/rspm/admin/python/

Recording these PyPI repository URLs when publishing content is essential to making it possible to use them to install Python package dependencies when the content runs on RStudio Connect.

title: `applications()` to return title field
description:
When deploying the app using Rstudio Publish widget user can specify an Title (appTitle). 

![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6959016/106907880-031f2b00-66ff-11eb-93b5-8964e9b4d8a2.png)


After deployment, on the (R)Studio Connect when listing deployed content the table shows a title. I wasn't able to find the name on the server.

![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6959016/106906701-bb4bd400-66fd-11eb-9b1a-8c43cd125334.png)
  

Then, when we use the `rsconnect::applications()` we get the `data.frame` with following columns: 
id, name, url, status, created_time, updated_time, guid, size, instances, config_url - but no app Title here

We would like to get deployed app title using `rsconnect::applications()`. Instead, we use `app_name` and convert it to `App name` which isn't accurate in all cases and it is potential BUG generator.

Summarizing, would be great if `rsconnect::applications()` return the apps `title`.

Cheers

title: Republish button doesn't appear after deploying an Rmd with deployApp
description:
`deployApp()` is a valid way of deploying Rmd documents but after deploying an Rmd with `deployApp()`, the deploy button doesn't change from Publish to Republish. It does change if you use `deployDoc()` instead, which presumably means running `deployApp()` with certain arguments specified would work as well. I think it would be good if the button changed regardless of which function is used to deploy the document.

I stumbled upon this as I was using `deployApp()` to deploy an Rmds with runtime `shiny` and `shiny_prerendered`, e.g. learnr tutorial.

title: support using renv for generating deployment bundles
description:
We should allow users to opt-in to using `renv` when generating deployment bundles to be used in publishing scenarios.

To ease the transition, we would first implement what is necessary in `renv` to generate a compatible Packrat lockfile, so that the existing publication workflows continue to "just work". This would allow users to reap the benefits of using `renv` for deployments, even with Packrat running in the backend.

Eventually, in the future, the backend could also support deployments using an `renv` lockfile, but that's considerably more work.

title: Ignoring any selected local packages during deployment
description:
This issue was already stated on the stack overflow.
During deployment, manifest generator should allow (packrat) to ignore the existence of any selected local packages. 
This is an option in packrat, but rsconnect does not expose this option. 

The solution provided by Soren Havelund Welling was suggesting to update the PackratSnapshot() function to allow for this functionality. 

I will be very glad if you offer such functionality or provide response why you do not want support it. 

Stack overflow question:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53006625/rstudio-connect-packrat-and-custom-packages-in-local-repos

Thanks

title: rsconnect::appDependencies evaluates eval parameter in rmarkdown chunks and might produce warnings
description:
# Context
I have an rmarkdown file that uses the `eval` parameters in chunks to control which chunks get evaluated. The idea is for that specific application that the code envoking `rmarkdown::render` can control what chunks will be evaluated instead of the report itself in order to keep the login in the markdown file as small as possible.

# Problem
When `rsconnect::appDependencies()` is invoked it evaluates the code in each eval parameter and thus producing a warning. These warnings are in particularly genereted during deployments to RStudio Connect. / shinyapps.io. Nothing breaks though.

# Reproducible example

Create a file "test.Rmd" with a single chunk

````markdown
```{r test, eval=show_chunk} 
summary(cars)
```
````

then:

```
> rsconnect::appDependencies()
Error in eval(x, envir = envir) : object 'show_chunk' not found
```

Here is an example of how it is used:

```R
rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd", envir = list(show_chunk = TRUE))
rmarkdown::render("test.Rmd", envir = list(show_chunk = FALSE))
```

# Potential solution

* One option could be to `suppressWarnings` when evaluating `eval`, but this might have other unintented sideeffects.

title: utils::tar(tar="internal") can create invalid archives with long user/group names
description:
See https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=17871

rsconnect asks for the "internal" tar implementation to be used here:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/68bf6a7b5292de49ac6e75cfbd1a8c7feedbdc58/R/bundle.R#L238

This was done because some tar implementations create archives with poor file encodings: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/150 & https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/165

Unfortunately, the internal implementation is not always appropriate, so we want to create a way to opt-out.

title: Issue with renv
description:
Currently, when `rsconnect` builds a tar file to upload content to Connect, it inspects the `.Rprofile` file (if present) for the presence of `packrat`.  If it's there, it comments it out so that it does not conflict with Connect's use of `packrat`.

This same process needs to be done for `renv`.  If `renv` is sourced in `.Rprofile` then you'll end up with competing package builds (Connect's use of `packrat`) and the content's use of `renv`.

The code should look for:

```r
source("renv/activate.R")
```

in `.Rprofile` and comment it out if found.

`packrat` is handled here: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/40c162bf3c4cd9b10deed82e1df9ec1b0c107c1f/R/bundle.R#L29-L39

title: Tar files incompatible with Connect when UIDs are large
description:
When `rsconnect` is used to bundle content to upload to Connect and a large UID is in play (larger than 32K), the tar file created cannot be read by Connect.

The `rsconnect` code creates a temporary file to write to and passes this to the R `utils::tar` function (see `R/bundle.R`, line 238).  That function (in the core R library) takes one of two paths.  If the tar file passed is a string it will invoke the OS's `tar` utility.  Otherwise (as in this case), it will build the tar file in the R code.

If you look in `src/library/utils/R/tar.R`, line 479, you'll see where the R code deliberately mangles large UIDs.

One possible workaround would be for `rsconnect` to create the temp file, immediately close it and pass it **by name** to `utils::tar()` but that could have all sorts of interesting and possibly unpleasant side effects.  Would it work on Windows?  It might if installing R also installed a `tar` executable...

title: deployments using older versions of foreign package produce spurious warnings
description:
When rsconnect checks to see whether a package is available on CRAN, it does so by checking whether the latest-available version of that package is available on CRAN:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/40c162bf3c4cd9b10deed82e1df9ec1b0c107c1f/R/dependencies.R#L83

However, the default filters (which define an inclusion / exclusion criteria for the packages returned by `available.packages()`) are left on. From `?available.packages`:

> Argument filters can be used to select which of the packages on the repositories are reported. It is called with its default value (NULL) by functions such as install.packages: this value corresponds to getOption("available_packages_filters") and to c("R_version", "OS_type", "subarch", "duplicates") if that is unset or set to NULL.
> 
> The built-in filters are
> 
> "R_version"
> Exclude packages whose R version requirements are not met.
> 
> < ... snip ... >

The current source version of `foreign` requires R 4.0.0:

```
> db <- available.packages(type = "source")
> db["foreign", "Depends"]
[1] "R (>= 4.0.0)"
```

which implies that the aforementioned check would fail to see that `foreign` is a package available on CRAN, if the current version of R were older than 4.0.0.

Since this is ultimately just a warning, we could relax this check by removing the filters used by `available.packages()`.

title: Problems with writeManifest for RODBC due to latest having R version 4 dependency
description:
I'm encountering an issue with writing manifest files for RStudio Connect at present.

I think this is due to the latest RODBC requiring R version 4 - which means that the current version is unavailable in my current R version (3.6.3).

I think the `writeManifest` call is having problems due to the `available.packages` call on https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/40c162bf3c4cd9b10deed82e1df9ec1b0c107c1f/R/dependencies.R#L83

It causes a warning "Unable to find repository URL for package RODBC" and causes the manifest to output as:
```
    "RODBC": {
      "Source": "CRAN",
      "Repository": null,
      "GithubRepo": null,
````

which then causes the deployment to fail in RSConnect (via git deployment)

My workaround for this at present is to set `options(available_packages_filters = character())` before calling `writeManifest` - but it feels like `writeManifest` should somehow handle this problem internally - maybe by setting the `filters` in the call to `available.packages` or maybe by searching in 
the archives for each repo.

title: Bug: error if requireNamespace is used in function
description:
I have a function which contains following code:
```r
missing_pkgs <- lapply(packages, function(pkg) {
        if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) pkg

For now, I have to use hack like `eval(parse(text = "requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)"))`. I would appreciate if you could fix this bug.

title: Check packrat dependencies before uploading
description:
The packrat lockfile is created with `packrat::.snapshotImpl` and warnings about packages that could not be snapshotted, e.g. because installed from source, appear as warnings, but only at the end once the bundle was uploaded and consequently failed after quite some time of waiting.

To avoid this, I do the following:
```
options("rsconnect.pre.deploy" = function(appPath) {
  # fails if packages are not snapshottable
  packrat::snapshot(appPath, dry.run = TRUE)
})
```
Is it possible to add this check by default, i.e. put it right before the execution of the `preDeploy` function? I.e. here:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/40c162bf3c4cd9b10deed82e1df9ec1b0c107c1f/R/deployApp.R#L221

Another inconvenience with the current workaround is that this option is not picked up, even when put into the .Rprofile, when the app is deployed by clicking `RunApp -> Publish app` in the RStudio UI.

needed @Roche

Here, `pkgA` and `pkgB` are internal packages located inside RSPM. I cannot explain the `glmnet` warning but in the past this has not resulted in API failure. 

Interestingly, I do NOT get this warning when publishing the API the "traditional" way via the RStudio GUI "publish" button. My assumption is that the same (or similar) function was being called "under the hood" but there seems to be a difference here.

Additionally I set:

options(repos = c(internal_plus_cran = "https://rstudiopm.mycompany.com/internal-plus-cran/"))
```

The curious part, is the the "CRAN packages" within my RSPM repository *ARE* found! It's only the internal packages that are not. This seems to be the key feature to a solution, I just haven't been able to debug it yet.

title: User defined cookies / headers are overwritten
description:
For the purposes of my example, I have only tested with `libcurl`. However, hopefully we can remedy this issue with the other download handlers as well.

Straight invocation of `libcurl`:
``` r
hm <- curl::new_handle()
curl::handle_setopt(hm, .list = list(httpheader = "key:value"))
curl::curl_fetch_echo("http://localhost:32776/upload", handle = hm)$headers
#>                                                    accept 
#>                                                     "*/*" 
#>                                           accept-encoding 
#>                                           "deflate, gzip" 
#>                                                      host 
#>                                         "localhost:32776" 
#>                                                       key 
#>                                                   "value" 
#>                                                user-agent 
#> "R (3.4.3 x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 x86_64 darwin15.6.0)"
curl::handle_setopt(hm, .list = list(httpheader = "key2:value2"))

# NOTE: key:value missing
curl::curl_fetch_echo("http://localhost:32776/upload", handle = hm)$headers
#>                                                    accept 
#>                                                     "*/*" 
#>                                           accept-encoding 
#>                                           "deflate, gzip" 
#>                                                      host 
#>                                         "localhost:32776" 
#>                                                      key2 
#>                                                  "value2" 
#>                                                user-agent 
#> "R (3.4.3 x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 x86_64 darwin15.6.0)"
curl::handle_setopt(hm, .list = list(cookielist = c("key=value;key2=value2")))

# cannot see it here, but there are key=value; key2=value2 cookies defined on this request
curl::curl_fetch_echo("http://localhost:32776/upload", handle = hm)$headers
#>                                                    accept 
#>                                                     "*/*" 
#>                                           accept-encoding 
#>                                           "deflate, gzip" 
#>                                                      host 
#>                                         "localhost:32776" 
#>                                                      key2 
#>                                                  "value2" 
#>                                                user-agent 
#> "R (3.4.3 x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 x86_64 darwin15.6.0)"
curl::handle_setopt(hm, .list = list(httpheader = c("cookie:key=value")))

# cannot see here, but key2:value2 cookie is missing. Also, key2=value2 header missing
curl::curl_fetch_echo("http://localhost:32776/upload", handle = hm)$headers
#>                                                    accept 
#>                                                     "*/*" 
#>                                           accept-encoding 
#>                                           "deflate, gzip" 
#>                                                    cookie 
#>                                  "key=value; key2=value2" 
#>                                                      host 
#>                                         "localhost:32776" 
#>                                                user-agent 
#> "R (3.4.3 x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 x86_64 darwin15.6.0)"
```

<sup>Created on 2020-02-14 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

As you can see, the `httpheader` setting is not additive, but overwrites. It even overwrites previously specified `cookie`s. As a result, when we add the user's options here:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/fef0bf6ac300e9823e4d348dffa68bcaacc8ee37/R/http-libcurl.R#L9-L12

And then don't incorporate them later:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/fef0bf6ac300e9823e4d348dffa68bcaacc8ee37/R/http-libcurl.R#L121

Everything the user has specified gets overwritten.

Are there any other workarounds to specify arbitrary user-defined headers / cookies via `.rsconnect_profile`? This is something that we have a few customers stuck at when deploying to RStudio Connect (specifically when headers / cookies need to be specified to satisfy a proxy).

title: Support `renv.lock` and friends instead of detecting dependencies from source
description:
I've switch to using renv, and it's a huge improvement over packrat. It's much faster and more reliable.

Are there plans for rsconnect::deployApp() to support using renv.lock directly instead of detecting dependencies from source?

Motivation: I have a large rsconnect application. It currently takes 59 seconds just for rsconnect::appDependencies to run on a modern machine. 

Thanks!

title: No option to set visibility (private/public) when deploying to shinyapps.io
description: I think it would be really useful to have an option in rsconnect::deployApp() that enabled setting of public/private visibility. At the moment publishing to shinyapps.io defaults to public and if you want it to be private you have to then remember to set it in the dashboard manually afterwards while your application is already open to the public. Found 2015 post on the subject by @tareefk [here](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shinyapps-users/--CE88p_IxU) (shinyapps.io google group).

title: connectApiUser generates partial configuration
description:
The `rsconnect::connectApiUser` function doesn't appear to generate a usable account configuration.

```
server_url <- "https://connect.my-company.io/"
server_name <- "connect.my-company.io"
account <- "jeff.keller@my-company.com"
apiKey <- Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO_CONNECT_API_KEY")
rsconnect::addServer(url = server_url, name = server_name)
rsconnect::connectApiUser(account = account, server = server_name, apiKey = apiKey)
```
This generates the file
```
~/.config/R/rsconnect/accounts/connect.my-company.io/jeff.keller@my-company.com
```
with contents
```
username: jeff.keller@my-company.com
accountId: 0
apiKey: <REDACTED>
server: connect.my-company.io
```
Which doesn't work for publishing content to Connect. If I "reconnect" the account through the RStudio GUI, the contents of the `.dcf` file become:

```
username: jeff.keller@my-company.com
accountId: 3
token: <REDACTED>
server: connect.my-company.io
private_key:
           <REDACTED>

```

Which works fine for publishing. How can I use `rsconnect:connectApiUser` to publish content without authenticating via the browser?

**Software versions**
`rsconnect` v0.8.16
RStudio Connect v1.7.8-7
Build "1144ac9"

title: improve browser linter
description:
I suggest the regex used in `hasBrowserCalls` can be a little too permissive:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/0aafa8855bdd04db4640fd091575778146992b00/R/lint-utils.R#L6-L10

In an internal project, it falsely matched a function I wrote (`fake_browser`) that is not an interactive-only thing. I suggest the regex be tightened, perhaps just a word boundary: `"\\bbrowser\\([^)]*\\)"`.

Do you think this would be too-restrictive as a general case?

(In case it helps: win10, R-3.5.3, rsconnect-0.8.16, deploying to RSC-1.8.0

title: Add option for deployApp to error out if return is FALSE
description: We use deployApp in ci/cd pipelines on gitlab to deploy applications to RConnect. Currently, if there is an error during deployment on the deployment server, the job still runs to completion and "succeeds" in the pipeline because an error is not thrown. Would you be amenable to adding a package option e.g. rsconnect.error.on.fail = TRUE that would see if the return of deployApp is FALSE and then optionally error out? Happy to provide a pull request if that helps.

title: linting: identify different-case filenames on case-preserving, case-insensitive systems
description:
Would it be possible to offer feedback when using a case-preserving, case-insensitive file system and referencing on-disk files using different-case names? For example, we may have an on-disk file named `images/RStudio.svg` and then use it from an R Markdown document with:

```markdown
![](images/rstudio.svg)
```

This renders fine on a macOS system, for example, but will probably err if that same content is rendered on a Linux system. The image reference is non-portable.

File-system differences will cause problems when migrating code from RStudio desktop to RStudio server, for example, or when deploying code to shinyapps.io or RStudio Connect.

Could we attempt to identify these situations?

Note: We sometimes avoid this problem when deploying content, as the filename for detected dependencies uses the case from the Rmd source - and that case is preserved in the deployment bundle.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/362187/68310104-727e1900-007d-11ea-8da6-eb8e65399903.png)

The on-disk case is used when dependencies are manually included in a deployment.

title: Implement alternative to OpenSSL md5 hash
description:
A customer has had an issue with this code:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/7f8e877744fc576bb6c25d7ba33aeb3722ca3a12/R/rsa.R#L6-L13

In their installation, attempting to use md5 results in an empty string (my guess is that this is because they have a FIPS compliant OpenSSL which does not implement md5). When this happens, we wind up with an empty token ID `T`, which creates problems downstream.

We should implement some kind of alternative token generation mechanism when md5 doesn't work. It could be completely random (as it used to be), use an alternative hash mechanism, or use a different md5 source.

(Internal: See support ticket 38544).

description:

appPath<-file.path(getwd(),"myapp")

logs <- client$getLogs(application$id, 50)
cat(logs)

client$getLogs has only 2 params...

Regards,

title: writeManifest problem with RETICULATE_PYTHON variable
description:

Current _documented_ behavior:

title: Bug: writeManifest incorrectly handles GitHub packages in some cases
description:
I believe this is a bug in the dev version of the `rsconnect` package and the way it builds manifests. Specifically, in some cases a GitHub package can be misrepresented and Connect (1.7.6-6) will try to install it from CRAN / RSPM.

To reproduce:
- install `rlang` from GitHub
- options("repos") has RSPM & CRAN defined to be the same URL
- `rsconnect::writeManifest` with latest from GitHub
- use programmatic deployment

Build error: exit status 1

It only breaks programmatic deployment, as far as I am aware, because IDE deployment does not use this part of the manifest.json. Not sure what, if any, effect would be had on shinyapps.io.

A hacky fix on the `bad-manifest.json` using `jq`:

```
cat bad-manifest.json | jq '.packages |= map_values(. | (if .GithubRepo != null then .Source |= "github" | .Repository |= null else . end))' > manifest.json
```

title: Broken deployments on Windows - packrat/rsconnect conflict
description:
Hello,

Since upgrading to v0.8.15, deployments from my Windows development environments to RStudio Connect have started failing. The error message is:
```
arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 0
```
which I've tracked down to `rsconnect:::snapshotDependencies`. Specifically, I think the code introduced in #309 is the problem for Windows users - the use of `contrib.url` in
```
repo.packages <- available.packages(contriburl = contrib.url(repos, type = "source"),
                                    type = "source")
```
and
```
repo.lookup <- data.frame(name = names(named.repos), 
                          url = as.character(named.repos), 
                          contrib.url = contrib.url(named.repos), 
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```
The first instance of `contrib.url` specifies `type = "source"`, but the second uses platform default (i.e. win-binary). This means that in:
```
package.repo <- repo.lookup[repo.lookup$contrib.url == package.contrib, ]
```
there won't be a match on Windows, and `snapshotDependencies` errors.

Let me know if you need more details on this, happy to provide. I don't know if setting `type = "source"` in the second instance as well would fix this?

Many thanks as always for all your work!
Chris

title: FR: create a .rscIgnore files to ignore files from being bundled
description:
It is already possible to provide a `appFileManifest` in `deployApp` to list the files that should be bundle. 

I am often in the case like with `.gitignore` or `.Rbuildignore` : it is easier to tell what we don't want at all instead of listing everything we want. 

I would find it interesting to have a feature like that, a `.rscignore` file that would allow to always exclude some files to be bundled by `rsconnect`. 
This is like `.Rbuildignore` that prevent bundling in R CMD build.

We encountered this need in some scenarios where 
* we have projects that push in RStudio Connect 
* the development is done externally and the code is delivered in a gitlab. when tagged, it should be published in one of the url
* One person of the project in charge of deployment need to publish. This require to recreate the dev env and publish the file. Some files used in development do not need be be published but is is not easy to exclude them. 

Publishing unneeded file is not a problem, but can cause issues because they are scanned for dependencies and can increase the bundle size. 

What do you think ? 

In a way this issue relates to #342 about how to manage bundle files.

title: Deprecate MD5 as a checksum algorithm
description:
We currently use OpenSSL's MD5 algorithm to add content checksums in several places. Generally we use this wrapper:

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/e6a7248acfb76d81e2ffff0837c43c34c70bf959/R/utils.R#L218-L219

However, some systems, most notably RHEL, can be placed into a FIPS compliant mode. The version of OpenSSL on these systems does not include MD5 since it's not considered a secure hash algorithm. Consequently, enabling FIPS mode on these systems removes the content checksums and with them the ability to publish content to Connect.

We should deprecate MD5 as a hash algorithm for content checksums; SHA-256 would be a better choice.

(Internal note: see support ticket 36904)

title: Default recordDir is appPath not appDir
description:
Hi, 

I was trying to understand where records of deployment are written to. My use case is for internal use to deploy the pkgdown website to RStudio Connect. Currently, the `rsconnect` folder is inside the `docs` folder and not at the root of the package. not an issue per se but I find something odd: 

Doc is saying
> recordDir Directory where publish record is written. Can be NULL in which case record will be written to the location specified with **appDir**.

However, in the code we have
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/b1194acf79acdd1f207c77e898a33b2f380bdc60/R/deployApp.R#L190-L192
where `appPath` can be modified to `appPrimaryDoc` or `appSourceDoc`, so not always `appDir`

Should the documentation be improve or is there something wrong where the record is written ?  

Just for sharing, I use this to have the record file in the root directory
```r
# working directory is package root file
rsconnect::deployApp(
  "docs", # the directory containing the content
  appFiles = list.files("docs", recursive = TRUE), # the list of files to include as dependencies (all of them)
  appPrimaryDoc = "index.html",                 # the primary file
  appSourceDoc = "docs/index.html",                 # the source doc
  recordDir = '.', # folder where to write deployement records
  appName = "appName",                          # name of the endpoint (unique to your account on Connect)
  appTitle = "My app title",                         # display name for the content
  account = "myuser",                # your Connect username
  server = "myconnect.server.com",              # the Connect server, see rsconnect::accounts()
  forceUpdate = TRUE
)
```
Just in case there is something that I missed...

title: RMarkdown renders flexdashboard, but rsconnect doesn't
description:
`isShinyRmd` function seems to be stricter than however RMarkdown package detects shiny runtime and knows to do `rmarkdown::run` over `rmarkdown::render`. Therefore, it's easy to create a `flexdashboard` that renders fine locally, but will break on deployment to Connect. 
Reprex:
```
``` r
library(magrittr)
c("---", 
  "title: test", 
  "output:", 
  "  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:", 
  "    runtime: shiny",
  "---") %>% 
  writeLines("./test.Rmd", sep = "\n")

# knits fine in IDE
# breaks on connect deployment
rsconnect:::isShinyRmd("./test.Rmd")
#> [1] FALSE

c("---",
  "title: test", 
  "output:", 
  "  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:", 
  "runtime: shiny", # Difference is indentation of this line
  "---") %>% 
  writeLines("./test.Rmd", sep = "\n")

# knits fine in IDE
# works in deployment
rsconnect:::isShinyRmd("./test.Rmd")
#> [1] TRUE
```

<sup>Created on 2019-05-07 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>
```
Possible to make isShinyRmd friendlier? Maybe just a nice warning?

title: Add a "global" rsconnect preflight script
description:
Many customers have many R installations and many users. Managing a separate preflight script for things like unsetting proxy variables, etc. for each R installation seems excessive when a global option might be possible (e.g. `/etc/rsconnect.global` or something). I'm not sure whether there is precedent for this in the R world, but want to record it as a feature request.

Having a global preflight script would simplify common operations that cross users _and_ R installations _and_ projects. For example, `Sys.unsetenv("http_proxy");`

https://rdrr.io/cran/rsconnect/man/options.html (near the bottom)

description:
Via a customer support ticket, a customer who got publishing errors when diagnostics were on:

``` 
Error in rawToChar(fileContents) : 
  embedded nul in string:

----- Error stack trace -----
13: rawToChar(fileContents)
12: paste0("<< ", rawToChar(fileContents), "\n")
11: cat(paste0("<< ", rawToChar(fileContents), "\n"))
10: http(service$protocol, service$host, service$port, method, url, 
        headers, contentType, file, certificate = certificate)
9: httpRequestWithBody(service, authInfo, "POST", path, query, contentType, 
       file, content, headers)
8: POST(service, authInfo, path, contentType = "application/x-gzip", 
       file = bundlePath)
7: grepl(contentType, response$contentType, fixed = TRUE)
6: isContentType(response, "application/json")
5: handleResponse(POST(service, authInfo, path, contentType = "application/x-gzip", 
       file = bundlePath))
4: client$uploadApplication(application$id, bundlePath)
3: force(code)
2: withStatus(paste0("Uploading bundle for ", assetTypeName, ": ",  [...]
```

I couldn't repro myself, but it's clear that what's happening is that the debug code (which tries to show server request/response bodies) is trying to dump the application bundle to the console, which is gzipped and therefore has null bytes. We should make sure this debug code only fires for JSON bodies.

title: Public function to determine files for bundle
description:
Today our programmatic deployment workflow hinges on a handoff between an R user and a "deployment engineer":

1. R users commits code to Git
2. R user runs `rsconnect::writeManifest` to generate a manifest that describes dependencies, that manifest is committed alongside the code
-- HANDOFF --
3. Deployment engineer tars files from the repo and the manifest into a bundle
4. The deployment engineer calls some API endpoints to deploy the content

One weak spot in this handoff is identifying which files should be included in the tar file in step 3. 

In push-button publishing, a handful of helpful functions and linters identify these files for an R user. If these functions were made public, we could think about how R users can communicate the results of those functions to deployment engineers.

cc: @aronatkins  @nwstephens  @kellobri

title: Different servers on the same host are treated as the same server, with confusing information presented in the IDE
description:
Reproduction steps:

1. Have more than one Connect server running on localhost (or any other host), binding to separate ports. For example, `localhost:3939` and `localhost:5000`

2. Add an account at `localhost:3939`, and deploy content

3. Add an account with the same username at `localhost:5000`

4. Attempt to redeploy the first piece of content to the first server

The IDE will show this as, for example: `admin@localhost:3939`

Expected: Content should deploy to the first server

Actual: Content attempts to deploy to `localhost:5000` and fails.

title: writeManifest does not save the requirements.txt
description:
When executing `rsconnect::writeManifest` for reticulated content that does not have a `requirements.txt` already, it seems to generate a `requirements.txt` that has the python dependencies in it (I can see the file in the file hash).

However, it does not save the `requirements.txt`, requiring me to go create one for the deployment to succeed. We should definitely _not_ overwrite / change a `requirements.txt` that already exists, but if one does not, I think it would be a fitting solution to retain the `requirements.txt` as a file that the `manifest.json` is dependent on for deployment.

This hearkens back to when the `packrat.lock` file was required in the bundle, as well, which is a requirement that was recently removed. I think the better long-term strategy is for the `requirements.txt` file to not be required (have all necessary state stored in the `manifest.json`)... but until then, I think it is worth persisting the `requirements.txt` file.

title: "Object does not exist" - rsconnect should deal with its metadata being out of sync with the server state more gracefully
description:
When a piece of content has local `rsconnect` metadata that is stale (either because the content has been deleted on the connect server or the connect server has been rolled back / wiped), rsconnect surfaces the error from attempting to get metadata from that (nonexistent) piece of content on the server. Notably: "Object does not exist."

The only way to fix this currently is to blow away the `rsconnect` metadata directory next to the content. This is not great.

What we should do instead might be:

- Lean on the force publishing option that already exists to force publishing over a non-existent piece of content.
- In force publish mode, warn the user that the content disagrees with the server, plus the vitals (stale content id, etc.) so if needed an admin can cross-reference the audit logs.
- In interactive mode, warn the user same as above and ask if they'd like to continue anyway.
- In unsupervised, non-force-publish mode: error instead of warning as above.

title: error with connectUser when using http url redirected to https
description:
Hi, 

In my internal setup of Rstudio Connect I encountered a strange behaviour when testing to connect a user using the 'http' url not the https, but with my server configure to redirect to https. 

I reproduced in with beta.rstudioconnect.com

## Step to reproduce

```r
rsconnect::addServer('http://beta.rstudioconnect.com', "beta.rstudioconnect)
rsconnect::connectUser(server = "beta.rstudioconnect")
> Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
```

The error happens in `rsconnect:::getAuthToken` where at some point a `POST_JSON(service, authInfo, "/tokens", token)` is called. The response is

Browse[4]> response

So this is a redirect call that `rsconnect:::handleResponse` does not seem to handle as it goes in here

title: Not able to set the proxyauth option when using rcurl.
description:
One our our customers is trying to use rsconnect through a NTLM proxy. There is option that needs to be passed into rcurl when it's evoked in order to tell rcurl that it needs to authenticate through the proxy. This setting can be toggled on an existing `rcurl` instance by doing something like the following,

`RCurl::curlSetOpt(.opts = list(proxyauth = RCurl::AUTH_NTLM), curl=rcurl)`

The issue is that there is no way to inject this particular option into a rsconnect call because it generates a new set of options for each call and requires additional options to be passed in as individual parameters on the function.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/3fe3b4ba1f0ab4dca1d83619e0527bd7cfc5b40e/R/http.R#L511

Handling this in some more general way seem advisable. Right now there seem to be 172 parameters that could be set (`RCurl::listCurlOptions()`) so the current approach doesn't seem to scale well. 

A better approach might be to have a global option (maybe `rsconnect.rcurl.options`) that caller could set to add whatever parameters they needed to the call.

title: stop packrat from adding itself as an implicit dependency
description:
Supported by `packrat` since https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/pull/250

This change would reduce the number of packages installed by any one deployment.

It would also make testing local `packrat`+`rsconnect` changes simpler, as `packrat` would stop attempting to include a installed-from-source version of itself.

https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/13a515e5401ca2c7ca990f1aca432db47ecd5d5c/R/bundle.R#L637-L643

changes to:

```
  suppressMessages(
    packrat::.snapshotImpl(project = bundleDir,
                           snapshot.sources = FALSE,
                           fallback.ok = TRUE,
                           verbose = FALSE,
                           implicit.packrat.dependency = FALSE)
  )
```

title: bitbucket repository references not copied into package entry in manifest.json
description:
GitHub repository references are copied out of the `packrat.lock` structure and promoted to the package object in the `manifest.json`.
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/58795406fc728f256599d82178f3786a6da26570/R/bundle.R#L393-L394

We do not perform the same operation for packages installed from bitbucket.
packrat gained bitbucket support here:
https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/pull/481

@kippandrew - how will shinyapps.io react to additional package-level fields?

Related: https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/issues/502 (`RemoteRef` not promoted for GitHub packages)

description: The `deploySite` function takes `siteName` that falls-back to the name from the site generator then passed as `appName` to `deployApp` where it may fall-back to the basename of the containing directory. title: Provide way to supply cookies to be used during deployment
description:
Some proxies use authentication cookies to validate requests. If a user already has such a cookie, they have no way to use it when deploying content from RStudio; it's not even possible to hack it together using e.g. `.Rprofile` since the R process that does the deployment uses `--vanilla`. 

At a minimum, we'd need to expose and document `rsconnect::storeCookies` or a suitable front-end thereof to make this work, and update RStudio so that it can inject cookies into the R process doing the deployment. Alternately (or additionally) we could add some hooks to make it easier for arbitrary code to run prior to deployment inside the R session, to make it possible for organizations to resolve these kinds of edge cases on their own.

title: Simplify download-edit-redeploy workflow
description:
Right now, it's possible to download a bundle, edit it, and redeploy it to the same endpoint using the following steps:

1. Download the bundle using the Source Versions dialog and untar locally.
1. Edit and redeploy using:

```r
rsconnect::deployApp("content/path", server = "host", account = "username", appId = 1234)
```

Where `1234` is the ID of the downloaded app.

Things that make this less than awesome:

- Finding the app id is confusing. A downloaded bundle reads `app-<appId>-<bundleId>.tar.gz`. There is no cue distinguishing app ID from bundle ID other than position. 
    - The app ID is not included in the manifest; arguably it should not be, because the manifest identifies the content of the bundle and not the location where it is deployed.
- This workflow goes to a core collaboration use case that's likely to be repeated many times by many people with varying levels of familiarity with R, RStudio, Shiny/RMarkdown, and RStudio Connect. 
    - There might have to be IDE changes to get this to work as pleasantly as we'd like.

title: Allow deployment using API keys
description:
Right now, deploying content from RStudio to RStudio Connect requires setting up a token and associating it with a public/private key pair. It's secure, but it requires a lot of back-and-forth and several steps, including a sign-in to Connect from a browser window in the IDE which is surprisingly difficult in some customer installations.

This is a proposal to make it possible to set up Connect accounts which do not use public/private key signatures but instead use API keys (a concept Connect already supports). These are less secure all around but much more convenient to use, and we already use something very similar for authenticating to shinyapps.io. The proposed changes are as follows:

1. `connectUser` gains a new parameter, `apiKey`. If this parameter is specified, the API key is saved to the user's account information in lieu of a token and private key (hereafter TPK).
2. When signing HTTP requests, the HTTP methods will use the API key in lieu of the TPK if the account being used to deploy has an API key.
3. The `deployApp` method (and perhaps others that take an `account`) will accept an API key for its existing `account` parameter. If this parameter is formatted as an API key, then the API key will be used for deployment. This will make it possible to perform deployments without prior account setup.

When this work is complete, it is anticipated that some additional work will be needed in Connect to expose the account API keys, and in RStudio to make it easy to add an account using an API key as the authenticating mechanism in lieu of the TPK.

title: Separate manifest generation, bundle generation, and bundle deployment
description:
Is there a reason that `rsconnect` _requires_ building `manifest.json` for each deploy?  

I think it makes sense that if the user already had a `manifest.json` file (i.e. after downloading a `.tar.gz` bundle from Connect), then there should be no reason for them to reinstall packages in order to generate another one.  In theory, they should be the same.  

Adding a parameter which defaults to NULL but passes the output to `rsconnect:::bundleApp` and allows bypassing the `manifest.json` build should be backwards compatible and would make migrating content from one Connect server to another much easier.

Of course, I might be missing an obvious reason that this is not available as an option.  Not sure if `packrat/packrat.lock` file needs to be included in this discussion or not.  In the case that you have downloaded a `.tar.gz` from Connect, you should have that file ready to go as well.

title: Please add a function that clears the deployment cache
description: Currently, the only way to clear the deployment cache for an application is to delete the /rsconnect/shinyapps.io/your-username/your-project.dcf file.  It would be useful if `rsconnect` itself had a function for that, so the cache could be cleared from the console.

title: Expose more arguments in documentation of the "deploy" family of functions
description:
Some of the "deploy" family of functions have this signature:

```r
function(modelDir, ...)
```

where the dots are passed to `deployApp()`.

Some of these arguments are essential, so I think it makes sense to be more explicit. For example:

```r
function(modelDir, server, ...)
```

The `server` argument must always be supplied, so it will make the documentation easier to follow if the mandatory arguments are documented on every function in this family.

title: Lint calls to .libPaths
description:
Deployed content is usually executed in an environment that attempts to recreate the deploying user's configuration of packages/versions/R.

Modifying `.libPaths()` from within a Shiny application, R Markdown document, or Plumber API is likely to use paths that are not meaningful on the server.

Warn users about this likely problem.

title: Feature Request: Static content - package repository
description:

https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001157793-Static-Content-on-RStudio-Connect

It would be nice to have support for deploying internal packages. Currently, we maintain our own package repo and serve it via nginx on a separate server. But if users could deploy an updated version of a package directly to rstudio connect from their IDE (EDIT: and we had some extra support to manage that repo) that would save a lot of time and energy.

Could probably also do this by deploying a plumber API that would manage the repo. But this seems like the connect team's design space.

title: deployement of packrat managed application
description:
Hi, I try to understand how I could deploy to RStudio Connect a project with dependencies managament using `packrat`. If you have advice, feel free to share ! I open this issue to share my understanding and some strange behaviour. Without packrat, during deployement with rsconnect, it will be the system and user library that will act as reference for package snapshot version. It is fine in some case but for other I want to have dependencies with the project and I use a `packrat` project for that. I have a `packrat` folder, and I activate `packrat` before deployment so that project's libraries are taken into account. At the end, I manage to publish it, but it does not seem to be working properly. here is my insights. When I click on publish button in RStudio IDE, it does not allow me to add pakrat.lock file in the bundle. I said myself it should work another way as rsconnect uses packrat itself in the process. However, `rsconnect` does not find all my packages into my `packrat` library folder but some are used inside my global installation instead. My application is then deployed with the wrong package version dependencies - should be my packrat deps not my global package. the `getPackageRecordsExternalSource` function use `system.file` to find the path of description. It happens, after investigation, that if I have for some reason a package loaded in namespaces, that does not come from my packrat lib, this will be this global paths which comes first and take over the path of package in `.libPaths()`. that is the way `find.package` is working; This case happens when I use an external package with `packrat::with_extlib` that loads a package from global lib for some reason even if it is present in packrat lib.
getPackageRecordsExternalSource function ```r getPackageRecordsExternalSource <- function(pkgNames, available, lib.loc, missing.package, fallback.ok = FALSE) { lapply(pkgNames, function(pkgName) { # The actual package record that will be populated by below logic. result <- list() # First, attempt to discover the actual installation for this package. pkgDescFile <- system.file("DESCRIPTION", package = pkgName, lib.loc = lib.loc) if (file.exists(pkgDescFile)) { # If the package is currently installed, then we can return a package # record constructed from the DESCRIPTION file. df <- as.data.frame(readDcf(pkgDescFile)) result <- suppressWarnings(inferPackageRecord(df)) ```

I have to be very careful about what I am doing before deploying and I have to check if everything ok. Not easy. After that, it took me a while to understand that I can put my `packrat.lock` file in the bundle. (obviously using `deployApp` only as I cannot select this file from publish menu). Digging into the code, I saw that if I put this file in the bundle, it should look for dependencies inside it and no more try to find package using `system.file` and `find.package`. It prevents from previous situation ! great !
inferredPkgRecords has check.lockfile = TRUE [code](https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/blob/df5dd5b6cb9f72010e07ccd3f4f813ab036d42c2/R/snapshot.R#L197) ```r # For inferred packages (ie. packages within the code), we try to construct # records first from the lockfile, and then from other sources if possible # (CRAN, GitHub, source repository) inferredPkgRecords <- getPackageRecords(inferredPkgsNotInLib, project = project, available = available, check.lockfile = TRUE, fallback.ok = fallback.ok) ```

With this, the lockfile inside the rsconnect bundleapp is ok. However, when creating a copy of the desc files in the bundle, it looks for `DESCRIPTION` file with `system.file` and I have the same issue as my first observation. https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/a16b8485ee4c7d43842bf13ebed2d312410f2285/R/bundle.R#L557-L565 That is to say the bundle pushed to rstudio connect, has a correct lockfile and then has correct packages version installed but the desc folder does not contains the correct package version and info because it copied it from the wrong path found by `system.file`. I was expecting that the current desc folder in packrat dir was used for copy DESCRIPTION file. Not sure what these desc folder is used for but it does not look ok to me. In conclusion, there is something strange in what I am doing or in current `packrat` behavior. I have this use case of packrat managed app deployement, either when I want to publish a locally `packrat` managed app, or when I download a bundle for RStudio Connect, restore using the packrat.lock in the bundle, and want to push on another server with same dependencies. (in the download bundle, `desc` folder has incorrect file by the way, as I mentionned earlier.) Have you encountered such things ? What are the correct workflow to push packrat managed project using `rsconnect` ? _(If I manage to create a reproductible project, I will add this to show the different behavior)_

Consider handling 404 errors explicitly with a more informative message or actually removing the dcf file itself.

title: Should we use `RCurl::base64Encode` vs. `base64enc::base64encode`?
description:
See: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/master/R/rsa.R#L10 and others

Both packages are available for use in `rsconnect`, because `base64enc` is a transitive dependency of `PKI`.

Should we be using the `base64enc` package for encoding things in base64? 

My instinct is that a single application ought not to use multiple implementations of the same algorithm if at all possible.

@duncantl notes in `omegahat/RCurl` -> `RCurl/base64.R`:

```
# There is some support for this in caTools but 
# that didn't install on some of my machines 
# and so we add it here since it is already available
# from libcurl and so is a natural facility in RCurl.
# I don't like duplicating functionality in other packages
# and discourage it. 
```

Ironically, this means that `generateToken()` calls `PKI.save.key` which calls `base64enc::base64encode` here: https://github.com/s-u/PKI/blob/bd7da17f207cd8a436811664e15a8cabe613cfe2/R/rsa.R#L86

And then immediately calls `RCurl::base64Encode` itself. It seems like we ought to be leaning on the same base64 encoder all the way down. However, if this code isn't robustly unit tested, maybe implementing those tests should be the first step before migrating encoders.

title: Emit `X-Auth-Token` HTTP header in every request to RStudio Connect
description:
Currently, we include the `X-Auth-Token` HTTP header on authenticated requests to RStudio Connect. 

On some configurations, however, a proxy may use the `X-Auth-Token` header in order to determine whether a request needs to be authenticated by the proxy. Making a request that omits the header in the presence of such a proxy will result in the request being redirected to e.g. a login page. This causes our unauthenticated requests (such as those to `server_settings`) to fail.

To make it easier to configure proxies, we should include `X-Auth-Token` every HTTP request we make to RStudio Connect servers, even those which are unauthenticated; we can use a dummy value such as `X-Auth-Token: none` to indicate that no auth token is present.

title: Emit a warning when deploying a bundle that itself contains rsconnect
description:
If a user accidentally saves a file with `rsconnect::deployApp` and deploys it, the application will fail to run after it was deployed. It would be nice if the act of deploying issued a warning, as it is atypical for a deployed application to deploy another application.

See https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shinyapps-users/_8VZM5gMUXM/dNOrDAKbBwAJ

title: Documentation request - showLogs()
description:
It would be helpful if the documentation for `showLogs()` included some examples.

First, it's not clear whether this is supposed to be something run in the local RStudio console (my guess) or included somewhere in the Shiny app code.

Second, it's not clear how to specify the parameters, particularly whether they have leading or ending slashes, whether to include `https://` and so on.

title: Output object can't share the same name (with different capitalization) with file in app folder
description:
This issue is related to https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/5565386d2de92f50cc3c8b4a56f0146d88609ec0/R/linters.R#L136.

Here is a MWE Shiny app:

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(),
    mainPanel( 
      textOutput(outputId = "description") 
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$description <- renderText({ "hello" })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

In the same folder as this `app.R` file is also a `DESCRIPTION` file, where the name of the file is in capital letters.

The app runs fine locally, however when deploying to shinyapps.io I get the warning `"Filepaths are case-sensitive on deployment server"`. And it points to the line with `      textOutput(outputId = "description")`.

Changing the name of the output to something other than description, or writing it in all capital letters to match the filename gets rid of the issue, but neither of these seem ideal.

title: appDeploy fails on (public) GitHub pkg dependency with HTTP 401: Unauthorized
description:
Consider the shiny MWE shipping with RStudio, plus some random dependencies:

```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)  # this works, even when installed via install_github
# library(pensieve) # this fails
# library(rlang) # this fails, when installed via install_github (latest version) but works when installed via install.packages

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

title: Warn when Shiny app has a `DESCRIPTION` file
description:
Repro:

1. Create a Shiny application which uses a library not part of Shiny, such as `library(plumber)`
2. Add to its directory a `DESCRIPTION` file which looks like a package's `DESCRIPTION` file 
3. Publish the application

The application publishes, but doesn't work on the server since it's missing the `plumber` library.

Here's an example `DESCRIPTION` that's known to be problematic:

    Package: placeholder
    Title: Does not matter.
    Version: 0.0.1
    Imports: bookdown
    Remotes: rstudio/bookdown

The problem is that when there's a `DESCRIPTION` file, packrat uses the packages named in that file instead of scanning the code for dependencies. This happens in packrat here:

https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/blob/f29ca870a6254859de034b7a811f31f5e9caa4bc/R/dependencies.R#L55-L81

We could fix this in a couple of ways:

1. Omit DESCRIPTION from the directory while packrat is scanning the directory. 
2. Add a flag (or environment variable, etc.) to packrat's snapshot that indicates that the directory should not be treated as a package even if it looks like one.

title: RCurl doesn't respect system certificate store
description:
We ship our own set of CA certs with rsconnect, and [use them when publishing with RCurl](
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/4a342a429cc7fdcb585a26186d5d013b35ce9f6e/R/http.R#L291). This is necessary because not all systems have the root CA needed to trust `shinyapps.io`; specifying our own set of certificates ensures that publishing to our cloud services will always work.

However, this option doesn't add to the system list of certificates -- it replaces it, as documented in [CURLOPT_CAINFO](https://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_CAINFO.html). Consequently, if customers want to supply a cert to be used with rsconnect--for instance, a self-signed certificate for a local RStudio Connect server--it isn't possible to do so elegantly; instead, it is necessary to individually update the PEM files per user, per R version, [as documented on our support page](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/115006524187).

We should respect both the system cert store *and* our own internal set of certs, so that customers can add their own certificates. Alternately, if this is infeasible, we should use an R option or environment variable to allow customers to add a cert store to our list.
