title: Feature Request: `showProperties` returns size in bytes of app bundle
description:
When running an account for multiple users, to ensure fair usage we have a "maximum shiny app size" that we enforce as much as possible.

It would be useful if the `showProperties`function of `rsconnect` could return the actual byte size of an app bundle, as we could then routinely delete apps which flaunt our maximum file size.

The bundle size isn't included in the shinyapps.io dashboard itself, so it may be that this data is not easily surfaceable to the rsconnect API. However, for many users I think it could be a useful metric to return.

Cheers

title: support pacman in library loading and installation
description:
I like to use [`pacman` ](https://github.com/trinker/pacman)for loading packages, because I can write this and share my code to others. 

```
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(shiny, DT, data.table)
```

They can just run the code and install packages they don't have automatically. If I used `library()` they will need to find every missing package and install them manually before the script can work.

However this doesn't work when deployed to shinyapps.io. Because shinyapps only look for `library` to install packages, and there is a explicit `install.packages` call in the script which is not allowed in shinyapps.

Right now I'm deploying my shiny apps both in shinyapps.io and github. People can run my app in github directly with `shiny::runGitHub`. Because of this limit, I cannot use the pacman lines in my code which make the github deployment less perfect.

Is it possible to extend shinyapps to support this usage? It should not be hard, just

1. ignore the install.packages line since it will never success anyway
2. scan the packages in this script. Just add `pacman` and all packages appeared in `p_load` call to the packages dependency list.

Thanks!

title: add native CI function to RStudio Connect / rsconnect
description:
I'm a huge fan of RStudio Connect, and I'm hoping we'll purchase it soon.
I just wish it would _also_ include tight integration with git(hub) (or some other SCM), and act as a CI service.

It might otherwise seem handy and work for smaller projects, but for bigger/more complex scripts, deploying from RStudio without checks and tight SCM integration seems a little scary to me.
(I, or someone else, will inevitably push something broken onto RStudio Connect).

I understand that I can *already* [deploy programmatically](http://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/appendix-rstudio-connect-deployment-guide.html) to RStudio Connect with `rsconnect::`, so we're going to use some Travis CI now.
However, this setup seems a bit suboptimal to me:

1. it's a bit tedious, because I have to manage *two* build environments with (CI and Connect), both with dependences etc.
2. At least (hosted) Travis kills the "on-premise" advantage of Connect, enterprise editions are *really* expensive and overkill. (Jenkins might be easier to use on-premise).
3. (At least) Travis isn't entirely trivial to get to work with R when more demanding dependencies come into play (partly because Travis is based on `precise`?). So anyway, Connect *already* has/needs a proper R build environment, so it'd be great to use this twice.

So, I'm really dreaming of a day I can ditch the separate CI.

**Does this make sense to anyone else, or am I thinking about this / using it all wrong?!**

@ajmcoqui gave me invaluable feedback on a related support issue.

title: Add support for multiple 'lucid' (shinyapps.io) servers
description:
Originally via request from @jspiewak. Currently, the shinyapps.io server is a singleton -- we always have exactly one. If you want to deploy to a different one (say, a local or staging server), then you set the `rsconnect.shinyapps_url` option to point where you want to go. This however is clumsy and makes it difficult to deploy from the IDE. 

The proposal is roughly to make lucid servers symmetric with Connect servers: that is, it should be possible to have several of them, with a M:M relationship to accounts. Towards that end the following changes should be made:
1. Add a new parameter to `rsconnect::addServer` which indicates whether the server being added is lucid or Connect (in a more user-friendly way, of course!)
2. Store the server type alongside the server URL (in the DCF file in `rsconnect:::serverConfigDir()`)
3. Return the server type in `rsconnect::servers()`. 
4. When creating a client, use the stored server type to create a client of the appropriate type (rather than relying on the server URL to infer the client type)

This will make it possible to have multiple lucid servers, and will make the undocumented option `rsconnect.shinyapps_url` obsolete. 

It will also require a symmetric change on the IDE, which has special behavior attached to the `shinyapps.io` server that will need to be applied to any server of type = lucid, and contains several assumptions that there's only one lucid server (internal bug to be created to track this).

title: rsconnect.max.bundle.size is too low for some shinyapps.io accounts
description:
shinyapps.io accounts with the Basic plan and above are allowed to deploy application bundles up to 3GB in size, but the `rsconnect.max.bundle.size` defaults to 1GB.  If these shinyapps.io customers attempt to deploy application bundles that are between 1GB and 3GB in size, the deployment fails even though they are within their shinyapps.io plan limits because they hit the `rsconnect.max.bundle.size`.  The workaround is to set the `rsconnect.max.bundle.size` explicitly to allow a 3GB upload:

`options(rsconnect.max.bundle.size=3145728000)`

However, this is inconvenient an non-intuitive.  Since the goal of this setting is to prevent the accidental deployment of enormous directory trees, we could safely bump the default value up to 3GB to avoid the shinyapps.io deployment problem while still preventing an accidental massive deployment.  If a shinyapps.io customer has a smaller plan and attempts to deploy an application bundle that is within the 3GB rsconnect limit but larger than her shinyapps.io plan limit, shinyapps.io will reject it at the server, so the risk to this change seems small.

title: manifest.json is missing generated index.htm from files property
description:
The `index.htm` file is created by writeRmdIndex:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/0a350894eaf4c7addb9424cad03a4f0348132461/R/rmdindex.R#L4

which is called from `bundleApp`:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/aac8077b3d9d0d056d75e42093e70ad1d757ac38/R/bundle.R#L67

Unfortunately, this is after we create the `manifest.json`:
https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/aac8077b3d9d0d056d75e42093e70ad1d757ac38/R/bundle.R#L59-L64

As a result, the `index.htm` file is not included in `manifest.files` and therefore never makes it into the Docker container used by shinyapps.io when running the application.

title: Should reject deployment to shinyapps.io if the app uses a package that requires access to the display
description: Shinyapps.io does not support any package that requires access to the display.  A user can deploy an app that uses one of these packages, but when they use the app in shinyapps.io, they see errors in the log and “Disconnected from server” in the UI.  It would be good to maintain a blacklist of known packages, detect when such a package is in the app, and surface a user-actionable message during the deploy process.

title: At deploy time, detect and warn when an Rmd file contains relative paths in directories above it
description: In shinyapps.io, you cannot load an Rmd file that contains relative paths in directories above the one in which the Rmd file resides; the relative paths must be at the same level or below. You can use these uphill references locally, but after deploying it, loading it fails.  Users find it confusing to be able to compile a .Rmd file using resources from directories above the one in which the .Rmd file resides, only to have it fail during deployment.

title: On deploy, should warn when code contains a setwd() statement
description: For apps going to shinyapps.io, at least, there is no need for a setwd() statement since the app is expected to be isolated and self-contained.  rsconnect allows you to deploy code that contains a setwd() call, but the app then fails on shinyapps.io during runtime.  At deploy-time, a warning about setwd() statements would be appreciated.

When trying to deploy a shiny app that depends on a non-CRAN/self-authored package to [shinyapps.io](http://www.shinyapps.io/) via `rsconnect::deployApp()`, I get the following error:

```
Preparing to deploy application...DONE

Ruft auf: <Anonymous> ... getPackageRecordsLocalReposImpl -> findLocalRepoForPkg
Ausf�hrung angehalten
```

Reading the [getting started manual](http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html) initially gave me the impression that package dependencies are automatically transferred/installed on [shinyapps.io](http://www.shinyapps.io/)

> Package dependencies
> 
> When you deploy your application, the rsconnect package attempts to detect the packages that your application uses. rsconnect sends this list of packages and their dependencies along with your application to the shinyapps.io service. Then shinyapps.io builds and installs the packages into the R library for your application. The first time you deploy your application, it may take some time to build these packages (depending on how many packages are used). However, you will not wait for these packages to build during future deployments (unless you upgrade or downgrade a package).

After reading the error message and thinking about, I rather suspect that my package must live in a publicly accessible repository. So I put it in my [`drat`](https://github.com/rappster/drat) repository and added the repository URL to `options("repos")`, but I'm still seeing the error.

title: improve "cannot connect" errors
description:
I noticed this when testing against a development server (so, it was frequently up and down), but felt like this could happen in other contexts and we could give better messaging.

I typically run the server within a Vagrant instance and port-forward from localhost:3939 to instance:3939. The side-effect of this is that there are different errors depending on whether or not the Vagrant instance is up.

Here is the error when the Vagrant instance is down. It is a hard connection-refused.

```
Preparing to deploy application...Timing stopped at: 0.003 0 0.008 
Error in function (type, msg, asError = TRUE)  : 
  Failed to connect to localhost port 3939: Connection refused
Calls: <Anonymous> ... tryCatch -> tryCatchList -> tryCatchOne -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted
```

Here is the error when the Vagrant instance is up but the server is down. It is a softer failure, probably due to how the Vagrant port-forwarding works.

```
Preparing to deploy application...Timing stopped at: 0.002 0 0.008 
Error in function (type, msg, asError = TRUE)  : Empty reply from server
Calls: <Anonymous> ... tryCatch -> tryCatchList -> tryCatchOne -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted
```

The difference in error is also visible just by hitting the endpoint with Curl.

I don't think the difference between these failures really matters -- we have good explanation text coming back from the network connection. What we should do is improve how we present this to the user.

title: deployDoc cannot handle pdf-generating Rmd
description:
This is perhaps part rsconnect, part rmarkdown.

Create an Rmd with the header YAML:

```
output: pdf_document
```

Attempt to deploy that document and you get an error:

```
> rsconnect::deployDoc("pdf.Rmd",account="dev")
Discovering document dependencies... 
 Show Traceback

 Rerun with Debug
 Error in (function (toc = FALSE, toc_depth = 2, number_sections = FALSE,  : 
  unused argument (self_contained = FALSE) 
```

This is because `rmarkdown::find_external_resources` eventually calls `rmarkdown::render` with `self_contained=FALSE`. This option is not accepted if `output: pdf_document` (see https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/437).

title: failing deployments still open app url and output error in an arbitrary location
description:
This is probably a mixed rsconnect/IDE issue...

I have a deployment that is failing for good reason - the target system is missing some OS dependencies.

The `Deploy` window has the message (in red):

```
Application deployment failed with error: exit status 1
```

That message does not appear at the end of the `Deploy` window but in an arbitrary earlier location (probably due to some stream buffering).

Further, I get a success message from the RStudio IDE and am sent to the application URL (this is at the very end of the `Deploy` window):

```
Deployment completed: http://HOST:PORT/USER/APPNAME/
```

The application URL justifiably 404s because the deployment failed.

I am surprised that:
1. The "deployment failed" message is not at the end of the `Deploy` buffer.
2. We open a browser and navigate to the application URL.
3. The `Deploy` buffer does not stay in focus (due to the error).

title: deployApp should inject shiny dependency
description:
server.R

```
shinyServer(function(input, output) {})
```

ui.R

```
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Hello Shiny!")
))
```

I can run the application in the IDE. I can deploy the application both with the IDE and manually via `rsconnect::deployApp`. In both bundles, we do not identify `shiny` as a dependency because it does not explicitly appear in a `library` statement.

title: `appmode` inferred incorrectly for multiple rmd files
description:
It sounded like the plan was to handle this in the IDE before we internally would call `deployApp`, but this sounded buggy to me. 

It looks like this code presumes that if a directory has more than 1 Rmd file, then it must be a Shiny RMD: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/blob/f59a6dfaf58b5f5b927606316c86ca03f1da4437/R/bundle.R#L79-L81

I had been deploying from a dir that happened to have two Rmds (though I was only interested in the `index.Rmd`, in this case) and couldn't get it to deploy as anything but a Shiny RMD.

Even if the IDE can do filtering to remove spurious Rmd files from the deployed dir, it is possible for Knitr to use child Rmd documents in a static mode (https://github.com/yihui/knitr/tree/master/inst/examples/child) so I think this is a legitimate use case.

title: deploySite possibly misleading
description:
Currently if I want to deploy a static website to rsconnect the best way I have found is using `deployApp`. If I were to use `deploySite(render = "none")` which seems to imply that I can deploy just the contents of a directory, I get an error

`No `_site.yml` found in docs.`

(note that technically my website is an rmd website, its package documentation, but does not have _site.yml)

This is because my website does not have this file, but `deploySite` thinks my site is an Rmarkdown site and when it cannot confirm that it errors.

I appreciate that the header of the documentation for the function does say "Deploy an R Markdown or quarto website to a server." but I think it's natural for a user to assume if they want to deploy a static website then the `deploySite` function would be the natural one. The python cli has an analogous `deploy html` which supports this. I guess the analogy to that would be deployDoc but that only supports one file at a time.

My suggestion would be to

a) Make it so that deploySite supports non rmd/quarto sites 
b) very explicit in documentation that only rmd/quarto is supported
c) make deployDocs which supports arbitrary upload of files.
